engagements.subject: CERES TAG data issue update
engagements.body: Good evening Karen, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since early April from your CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. Hello Karen! I you are going well and that the sampling with Ben went well last week! Its that time of year and I am putting together the second annual co-benefits report for the LRF. I’m seeking management info from you related to the activities outlined in the LRF, for the whole of the previous 12 months 1 Nov 23 - 31 Oct 24. Could you please send me any evidence or records of the following (including management records, photos, invoices, receipts, locations, a short description on each would be great!) - Weed management inc fire management if completed (location, size of area, timing, frequency) - Stock management/exclusion in remnant vegetation (timing, access, locations) - Stock restriction from riparian areas(timing, access, locations) - Feral animal management - Soil health – sowing multi-species pastures, planned grazing, compost tea (records of sowing, seed mix, timing, germination, grazing management records) - Employment and skills (contractor hours, upskilling, participation, local suppliers) Can you describe any positive changes to: - Soil health/erosion/water quality? - Vegetation? - Wildlife? - Employment and skills benefits? I’m compiling the report to send through to LRF by the 31 October. Please give me a call if you’d prefer to discuss! Thanks for your help!

Hi Karen, As discussed, Accounting for Nature have requested some extra details about you. Can you please review and edit the text below? Thanks About the Landholder (200 words max): Please provide us with a brief description of the Landholder. This may include information about themselves, their land, interests or motivations for developing an account. This will be published on the account page, alongside the ‘About Agriprove’ section. Please see Account 69’s webpage for an example of how this will look. The Scanlan’s are passionate about leaving their landscape in better condition than they found it and are actively working to improve biodiversity and increase native species on their property Kenmay Station. Thanks to their efforts over the last 9 years, approximately 60% of the property now has vegetation cover, with much of it being high quality remnant vegetation. The Scanlan’s use a holistic management approach to implement regenerative grazing practices and multi-species pastures, and also make their own compost tea to boost soil health and function. The Scanlan’s became interested in regenerative and holistic management through their involvement with a local producer group when they lived on the Sunshine Coast, who delivered workshops with guest speakers. Robert is also particularly interested in breeding the best genetics for the local environmental conditions and breeds high quality Drought Masters for breeding stock. “We want to leave our land better than we found it for future generations including our daughter, especially when we have Baffle Creek along our border which runs into the Great Barrier Reef.”

engagements.subject: Re: Fysh Project
engagements.body: Hi Claudia To answer your questions; 1. Grazing in riparian areas Cattle did not graze at all in riparian areas along waterways. In our three larger paddocks with remenant vegetation, cattle were withheld from November 2024 to the start of March 2025. For the other 8 months of the year cattle were rotated two weeks in and three months rest. This means that the cattle grazed the riparian areas for approximately 6 weeks during the year. 2. Sewing improved pasture In March 2025 30 hectares beside Baffle Creek was sewn to improved pasture. The seed mix consisted of humidicola, signal and rhodes grass. 3.Employees and contractors My husband and I employ two local contractors. One lives on the farm. They each work approximately 20 hours per week. Their primary tasks are weed control and slashing pasture. 4. Rainfall The rainfall over the past year was average, with increased frequency of showers. This was similar to last year. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Karen, I am getting in touch as I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. We complete this review each year to determine if we think re-sampling your carbon project would be worthwhile. This review uses satellite imagery to determine if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. This means that we will potentially resample your project this year as it has demonstrated positive indicators. To confirm this, we will now run your project through an additional model and complete an implementation check over the phone. Once we have that information, we can confirm if we will be resampling this year or not. Is there a time that suits you in the next few weeks to complete this review over the phone? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes set-up and next steps
engagements.body: Good morning Lance and Kylie, Welcome to the Tags for Tonnes team!! We are proud and excited to offer a world-first initiative such as this to assist with your carbon project management. Now that we have your tags on the way, we are progressing to have you set-up and ready by the time your tags arrive. Here is a short guide on how to operationalise your tags when you receive them: 1. The instructions will be on a small welcome card in your package - scan the QR code with your phone camera to access them. 2. Charging the tags in the sun is the first step to getting started (they will need to sit in the sun for 5-7 days to charge fully). 3. I have created an account for you in our software and have uploaded your farm boundaries in it. 4. We will need to jump on a video call so I can run you through how to connect your tags to our software - this will require making a Ceres Tag account in their portal, and registering your tags to our software (I will walk you through this step-by-step) . 5. Once your tags are charged and you are set-up in the software you are ready to tag 6. It is important to record as many details around which animal you are tagging (Ceres tag number, VID, NLIS ID, age) using what tag and what mob/class/breed they belong to. 7. Taking a picture of the animal is also an important step to help tell their story. 8. Once tagged, and the animal data is recorded we can jump on a call to set up your animal information in the 'My Herd' section of the software - this will power all the insights you can get on your herd's performance. 9. engagements.subject: Duncan CP 2 - Site Audit Visit - Tuesday 11th June
engagements.body: Hi Kylie and Lance, In preparation for the Site Visit on Tuesday 11th June, I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. Please see the attached agenda for the site visit, and a couple of aspects that will be discussed as well as the following questions. 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of FMR dates) 2. Detailed description of all lad management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the property, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to house/office - interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall, the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that management records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the management records such as livestock records and grazing charts * Confirmation that we (yourselves and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the carbon project operation, implementation and administration. Please reach out if you have any questions. Have a good weekend. engagements.subject: Ceres Tag data issues update
engagements.body: Dear Kylie and Lance, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since early April from your CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. engagements.subject: Questions from today regarding sustainability certifications
engagements.body: Good evening Lance and Kylie. Thank you for being so generous with your time today, I really appreciate it. As mentioned below are some of the questions we ran through, if you have anything to add please feel free to put them in and send them back. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? No, just organic stuff – don’t qualify (don’t breed, buy in and keep for under 2 years) They trade too much and not enough breeders – gotta have the cattle for more than 2 years Looked into it 10 years ago If no, then why not? Just haven’t got to it because of not meeting the organic cert qualification Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? No, haven’t looked into more Grass resilient certification have heard Reef credits – interested post development Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? Is ideal for them and they are very open to it They are practicing no hormone and non-synthetic feed Very, very interested Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? Quite interested as long as it doesn’t cost too much Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? Have looked at retailers Sell to Meat Works - shop around for pricing Go for premium price MSA Private sales – bulls (stud premiums) More for the quality than the environmental – organic is the only option (gone off that) Has enquired at beef expos for Auction Plus – is the way to go in the future (AI) – photos of property and cattle – price of putting on Auctions Plus is dearer than selling through the (Meat) Works but price is coming down Gotta have time to look at it properly – but has been very interested for the past 10-12 years What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? They are pretty well up there already More in the soils – more testing of soils to see what is lacking in soils Educating them on what the results mean and how to adapt and improve their place Some education and making the reports easy to understand We give a lot of information and they don’t know how to interpret Pointing out what is missing in the soils and how to improve using the tests we have done Microbial analysis to drive the limiting factors – key factor Thank you! engagements.subject: AgriProve - Eligible Interest Holder Consent
engagements.body: Hi Sonya and Fraser, One of the key components for project compliance and ACCU issuance is the requirement of all Eligible Interest Holders (EIH) to consent to Registering a project with the Emissions Reduction Fund. As AgriProve have recently become the proponent of Greenhill Carbon Project, yourselves as the landholders have become eligible interest holders. This consent form is required to be signed by all parties with "Eligible Interest" as per the land title on which the project is Registered. According to the title registered, GPC (QLD) PTY LTD must complete an EIH Consent form. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Greenhill Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Sonya and Fraser, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project, Greenhill Carbon Project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you would be happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the next few weeks? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding the resampling process. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I will call within the next few days to discuss your results and project, but if you have any other questions feel free to reach out to myself or any other member of the AgriProve team. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Casey Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Peter, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the baseline to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. At AgriProve we are continually improving and adding to the inputs to our models to provide more detailed and accurate project tracking. If there are any indicators that you feel would be particularly useful in assisting you in your project, please don’t hesitate to get in touch with me to discuss. You may already be participating, but I also wanted to reiterate that we are providing soil carbon information for our farming partners and facilitating sharing of knowledge via our Facebook AgriProve Carbon Builders Community group. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have gone over the last year for you on the property. I’ll attempt to contact you on your mobile in the coming days, but please feel free to reach me on 0408 448 190 at a time that suits you. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Peter, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. Here’s the link if you’d like to check out the program: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/ Hope to see you there, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile:+61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io

engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Peter, Next week at the conference, AgriProve will be running a session (Wednesday 5th Nov) called: Project Ecosystem in Action: The Carbon Farming Value Chain It’s a practical look at how the different parts of the soil carbon value chain work together - from the producer and input suppliers to the technology side and the market. The idea is to show what’s actually happening on the ground and how soil carbon projects turn into real outcomes for producers and the broader market. If you’re coming along, it’d be great to see you there or have a chat at the stand afterwards. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jack, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your projects to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached documents. Your projects had a very similar trend, but negative relative to the baseline period ( the baseline period had a higher average change). This suggests that its unlikely that enough carbon sequestration has occurred to measure an increase and therefore has not met our threshold for resampling this year. As it was close we will run it through some of our other models to determine if we might, but at this stage we will not be resampling your project this year. We will complete this review of your project again next year to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. Please note that this trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it is showing that the trend in vegetation greenness which is an indicator of carbon sequestration and in this case it has shown that its unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.body: Hi Alan Thank you for getting the initial documentation through, it is great to have you onboard and we’re excited to be working with you on your carbon farming journey. I have attached in this email a complied version of your Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement for your records. As next steps, I would like to introduce you to Dylan Jones, your Soil Carbon Project Co-Ordinator, who will work closely with you to finalise the details of your project, including: Verify your Land titles The soil carbon project area(s) - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, forested area and other infrastructure. We will also take into account areas for Avoided Clearing project work with GreenCollar. Project structure - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. Quote you on soil baseline sampling (your only project fee). - If your project area is suitable for the Hone grant, 30 baseline cores will be cover at no cost. I would like to set up a 15-20 minute video meeting to introduce you to Dylan and to validate our understanding of your farming operation and desired project areas. How are you placed for a call prior to the Easter long weekend? We can expect the project mapping component to take 1-2 weeks, and while not much is required from yourself, we will continue to check in, working collaboratively on the project design. Once complete, we will provide you with your final project maps, baseline quote and the Sales and Licence Agreement to be complete. Thank you again for choosing AgriProve as your trusted carbon partner, and we look forward to supporting you on your journey. As always you can reach out with any questions. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Result
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Alan, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? Tuesday or Wednesday next week would be ideal, but happy to work around you. One question, what is the likely cost to purchase or lease the unit after the first 12 months (and how does this tie in with Agriprove being responsible for soil sampling costs after day 1)? If I look at each of the lots for my Rye Park property (using maps.six.nsw.gov.au), I get the following results: Lot Approx. Ha Available for Project Comments 14 38 ~32 (~85%) house & sheds on this lot 60 120 ~114 (~95%) 57 37 ~22 (~60%) includes large wooded area 64 38 ~34 (~90%) 65 118 ~88 (~75%) ~25% wooded 163 18 ~14 (~80%) SUB TOTAL 369 ~304 126 94 ~80 (85%) wind farm lease: road, turbine, transmission lines 79 178 ~116(~65%) wind farm lease: transmission lines SUB TOTAL 272 ~196 GRAND TOTAL 641 500 (~78%) In the table above I have separated out the two lots that are under lease to the wind farm. In terms of new management practices that I will implement: * Use of fertiliser (not used for at least 10yrs according to the vendor’s IM)…if you look at googlemaps at neighbouring lots where fertiliser is used, it is pretty clear that using fertiliser will have a big productivity benefit * Mulching of woody weeds (particularly Lots 126 & 79 – these were locked up for a couple of years during wind farm construction with no livestock to chew down the woody weeds) * Crops & planting pastures (particularly parts of Lots 14, 60, 57, 126 & 79)…will do these pastures up slowly over time…currently all natural pastures * I am looking to run ~1,000 merinos + 50 cows (cows not currently run on the property). The internal fencing on this property is poor. If there is a benefit in fixing internal fences, allowing me to create smaller paddocks & move stock more often, I would like to do this. I think this is likely less than the historical stocking rate, but am not entirely sure I’m pretty good to talk most days – do you want to send me another Teams invite? Thanks & regards Michael Brown 0411322440 P.S. One more question…you had mentioned on our previous call difficulties if I wanted to sell a Lot that was part of a carbon project…I would like to better understand those restrictions. Hone Sampling - no idea what the cost of purchasing the equipment. The hone unit Sale of land during the project - they have the right to sell part or whole of the project area during the 25 year project. They need to let AgriProve know. The only issue is the payment of baseline sampling. Windfarm, nothing stopping you from doing this - we will need to vary the project area, to exclude the individual turbines. 1) Lease for $1 for the first year. After which the course of action has not been clearly defined but it is likely the landholder would have the option to purchase at ~$9500. Much changed here Barbara? No affect on the standard CFI sampling commitments from AgriProve as per our normal offering. 2. This is why we typically restrict projects to being within lots, that way if a lot is sold the project can go with it. Otherwise it would potentially collapse the proejct. You can however deregister entire CEA if needed but credits would need to be paid back. 3. In the case your refering too here Scott, the wind farm is leasing the property, but subleasing areas back for Agricultural production. My understanding would be EIH consent will be required, however the landholder is still on the title so should be ok.

engagements.subject: AgriProve - Project information
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, Thank you for your time on the phone today. It was great to get a few more details on your operation and discuss your soil carbon project opportunity. The next step will be to come out and take a look on the ground. As discussed, I'll aim for the afternoon of Monday 12th of August. I'll stay in touch to line up a more specific time of day as we get closer and to make sure it still works with you. If anyone else from your Somerton producer group would be interested in a conversation, feel free let them know I'll be in the area. I have attached below the engagement document to move forward with mapping finer project details. No need to do anything now, I can talk you through these further when we catch up, but it is always useful to understand the next step and have the information in advance. To engage AgriProve in project mapping we require the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement document to be complete. It is free and non binding to progress through mapping however, it serves a few purposes: • It engages AgriProve to begin the project scoping process and is an agreement you will not engage with another party while we commit resources to this. • It specifies the eligible activities to be registered with the projects should you decide to proceed and collects the 5-year baseline management practices for your property. This information is required to determine that eligible activities are new or materially different and is required to register your project. I have also attached our Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects, detailing how your project(s) are managed and monitored by AgriProve while ensuring our landholders maintain full management autonomy. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. I will send through the commercial terms in another email so keep things tidy. Please feel free to reach out for any questions and I look forward to speaking further soon. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Project Scoping kick off
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, ​Thank you for taking the time to complete the engagement documents with me. I look forward to getting your project scoping underway. To get started please finalise data entries, review, sign and return the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement form we prefilled yesterday (attached). I have also attached our Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects detailing how your project(s) are managed and monitored by AgriProve while ensuring our landholders maintain full management autonomy. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. Once returned, you’ll be assigned a dedicated Soil Carbon Project Officer and we will begin our project scoping process by: 1. Verifying your Land titles 2. Defining the soil carbon project area(s) - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, heavily timbered areas and other infrastructure 3. Designing project structure - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. 4. Provide a quote on soil baseline sampling (your only project fee). 5. Provision you with our Sales and Licence Agreement to move forward. I look forward to working with you further and congratulation on getting started. engagements.body: Good morning Leonie and David, Congratulations on your recent ACCU issuance for Ryan Carbon Project 2 and thank you for your patience. The statement outlines the following areas: * AgriProve Carbon Project Licence Fee due to Client (Agriprove pays $1 per year to you as a landholder for the 30 year Carbon Project period) * The ACCUs Issuance * Balance of ACCUs after Agriprove Success Fee (25% success fee on total ACCUs issued) * Balance of Baseline Soil Sampling cost across all projects * ACCU Distribution preference (as outlined in the KCT) Please also see the attached bank details request form. We require this information to pay the $30 (excl. GST) licence fee to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon project for the term of the agreement. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 ACCU Issuance
engagements.body: Hi Leonie, I think that you are referring to the cash prepayment option for ACCU distribution, where AgriProve makes a cash prepayment for ACCUs to the project operator in advance of the ACCUs being generated at a fixed price of $12.50 per ACCU. This option would be selected at the start of the carbon project in the Sale and Licence Agreement and is based on the prepayment to AgriProve at an agreed price of $12.50 for ACCUs from a buyer. Based on your selection of option 3 in the Sale and Licence Agreement to 'hold ACCUs for future sale', your ACCUs will be held in AgriProve's Registry of Emissions Units Account (ANREAU) on trust for sale at a later date nominated by you for the best price available. AgriProve will act as a market broker for the ACCUs, and a brokerage fee of $0.375 per ACCU will be charged. These ACCUs could also be transferred to the Operators stand-alone ANREU account if established. Sent email to notify Leonie her emissions data had been fixed in the platform Hi Leonie & David, Thanks for your patience. I’ve now updated your account with stock movements that we went through together 2 weeks ago. We’ve fixed the issues with weights and the emissions outputs are now looking a lot better. Here’s a snapshot I took of your emissions page. You’ll notice Emissions Intensity for beef are on the low side (which is good)- a typical regen beef operation will run at 9-12kg CO2/Kg liveweight compared to say, 12-18kg CO2/Kg LW for a feedlot operation so you’re doing well! I suspect it might come up a bit once we start adding years before and after to smooth out the end of year trading. Sheep meat Emissions Intensity is about average (typically 6-12kg CO2kg LW) but again I think we’d see some smoothing out as your trading was right at the end of the year and including the following year would give us some more accuracy. Your Scope 1+ 2 emissions are correct and can be used for reporting to any downstream suppliers if that’s what you're intending to do. Look out for more updates in the coming weeks as we add status reporting for your Carbon Project. Also, regarding your ACCUs balance- this is the total issuance form the ACCU scheme and doesn’t include AgriProve’s portion. We’re looking at adding a ‘wallet’ feature in the future that splits these numbers out and tracks subsequent issuance and spend eg, with Clima. We let you know when this becomes available. Any other questions please feel free to reach out to myself or Claudia. Regards,

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Paul, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Record's & Update
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Paul, Thanks for your time on the phone today. As discussed, the next steps will be: 1. We are going to vary your start date till after your baseline period - This has no effect on you other than giving us all more time to get the records together for the 5-year deadline. This may also be an advantage as it will push out your sampling to April next year and it may not be as dry as it is now. 2. Early next year we will put your project through our new model to get a better indicator of if carbon sequestration has been likely and look to schedule your 5-year sampling. Our operations team will be in touch when that is done and they are organizing the logistics. ( I expect that to be in February/March). * 3. From Now we will start pulling together all of your records for you to complete the 5-year audit. There are a few steps to this, but as a start we need to get together your management history from before the baseline period and then now the 5 years since the project has started. TO GET STARTED WITH THE RECORDS: What we need to prove is that you have done things differently since commencing the project ( start date 19/01/2021) - focusing on your nutrient application, what you have sown and anything that could have improved carbon like lime, fencing and grazing management. To do this, we basically need WHAT was done, WHEN and WHERE. E.g. 50kg of Urea/ ha was applied to paddock 1 and 2 which is a total of 150 ha and ideally with evidence eg. receipts - the more detail the better as a change can be you used to apply 100kg and now you do 50kg, you used to apply it in 1 form and now you've put it out as something different, you used to sow oats and now you do a mix, you used to do a summer mix and since starting you've put in a winter mix ect. - the practice change doesn't need to be the same across your whole place, but something different does need to be shown across your whole project. So as a starting point: * if you could get together those rudimentary notes about what was done in each paddock over the time since you had the farm ( as detailed as possible like mentioned above) * A paddock map would be great if you have one ( can be simple drawn or photo ) so we can visually understand what has happened where from those notes. Once we have an idea of this - we can make a plan of attack and let you know what specific evidence you need. If you have any questions feel free to give me a call anytime. engagements.body: HI Paul, Thanks for that. I will get the forms for you to sign in the next week as Its very simple with no bank. For the records: You have sent 2021 till now which is the current 5 years which is great thankyou. We do though need records for the 5 years before that too (2016-2020). Eg. just write down Farm purchased in 2018 ( if they need proof we can get that later), then we need what you did for the first few years before starting the project. If that is not a lot that's okay but we need specifics of what that little bit was. The reason is - the main thing you have to prove to the regulator is that you are doing something NEW/different since starting the project. Your 2x activities are reestablishing and rejuvenating pasture by seeding or pasture cropping and applying fertilizer. We need to show how the fertilizer you have been doing is different to before (eg. rates, forms and types) and what you have done since starting the project with pasture improvement. (fertilisers, rates, and any pasture improvements eg. reseeding) Once we have this to compare it to we can figure out how to show a change in practice to the regulator. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Result
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jodie, As discussed, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. This review uses satellite imagery to determine if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. This means that we will potentially resample your project this year as it has demonstrated positive indicators. To confirm this, we will now run your project through an additional model and complete your implementation check over the phone. Once we have that information, we can confirm if we will be resampling this year. Is there a time that suits you in the next few weeks to complete this review over the phone? Talk soon. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Perkins Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Jane, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the baseline to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. You may already be participating, but I also wanted to reiterate that we are providing soil carbon information for our farming partners and facilitating sharing of knowledge via our Facebook AgriProve Carbon Builders Community group. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have gone over the last year for you on the property. I’ll attempt to contact you on your mobile in the coming days, but please feel free to reach me on 0408 448 190 at a time that suits you. engagements.subject: Perkins Carbon Project Update
engagements.body: Good Morning Jane, I have checked in on your project for you. As mentioned in my previous email, I have completed your annual review and the result is attached. This is showing that relative to the 5 years prior to baseline the NDRE has had a negative trend and has not met our threshold for resampling this year. If you want to continue with your project, we need to resample regardless of what this trend indicates as we need to complete the 5-year reporting. What we can do is we can apply for a variation on your project which would give us 18 more months before the reporting is due. This would give you 18 more months to decide what you want to do, the carbon to increase and to get all the auditing documentation together if you did decide to continue. If you don't want to continue, there will be a fee of $4995. This fee is not from us, it is because you received that amount in advanced payment from the Clean Energy Regulator at the beginning of your project. This needs to be repaid to them for everything to be finished with your project. If this payment is an issue we can possibly explore extending the date as mentioned to give you more time to pay it, but I would need to check with the team if this is allowed. What are you thinking you want to do? Feel free to give me a call anytime to discuss. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Greenhill Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Sonya and Fraser, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project, Greenhill Carbon Project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you would be happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the next few weeks? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding the resampling process. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I will call within the next few days to discuss your results and project, but if you have any other questions feel free to reach out to myself or any other member of the AgriProve team. engagements.body: Hi Mitch, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. QTR Check - 16/01/2025 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1 . Please Cross check the eligible activities that were chosen by the landholder at the time of project registration are accurately captured against customer deal in HS: · Applying nutrients · Re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture · Altering the stocking rate 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 6 months? Applying nutrients via drone or buggy Winter planting of March to June - rye, oats, lucerne, chicory, lupin, clover, radish, plantain - exception results Mowing paddocks infront or behind the cattle - grazing smaller areas for more trampling and intense grazes 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 6 months? Winter planting again Leaky weirs in the gully 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Grazing smaller areas 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% 50% ~30ha of nutrient application and pasture planting 100% grazing 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} 8-12 hrs 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} 14-36 day rotation 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 6000m2 - 8000m2 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? No - what does he need record of 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? more biodiversity more wild life haven't treated for flies or ticks for the past 3 years 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? dry period last year until november - sold a lot of cattle in relation to this 12. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Noel, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a positive trend since baselining . This means that we will potentially resample your project this year. We have an additional model that we will now put your project through to assess if we should sample that we will be running now, and we need to complete and implementation check in call to tick of the requirements for this year. engagements.subject: HORIZON Model Check in
engagements.body: Good Morning Noel, Thanks for your time on the phone yesterday. It was good to chat to you again. I have looked into your query about the HORIZON model. As I mentioned on the phone the HORIZON model is currently predicting a decrease of 500 t of carbon. This seems unusual due to you having a positive lead indicator last year, a good season, HORIZON layer showing mostly strength on your platform map and you have seen improvements in your soil tests. In looking into it - the model is noting a very low confidence in this prediction. This could be due to the small size of the project, location or potentially it just not having enough data points in your area. The team are going to look into this a bit more deeply to see if they can narrow down exactly why this might be and make a plan of attack going forwards. At this stage the intention is to still go ahead and put you in the schedule 2 group as discussed. Once they figure out what the reason for unusual result is they may decide to resample your project as normal this time - which should then give the model more calibration to be accurate going forwards or anywhere in between depending on the cause. The groups aren't expected to start running till June so just a heads up that you may not hear a confirmed answer on this till at least then depending on which group you fall in. E.g. If you are in group 2 it may be even later than June before they lock in the plan. I will keep checking in on this for you. Know it is moving and we are going to look into finding whatever solution works best for your project. If you have any questions- feel free to give me a call anytime. engagements.body: Hi Bill, Thank you for the information attached. I just were contacted by Pierre (a contractor) for soil sampling the property. I explained to him that the property is currently not accessible as the autumn break have arrived for us. Our property is a very special project as only certain times of the year is safe to entry due to its layout. Also just finished sowing some paddocks so I was not planning to take any further samples for another 2 or 3 years from now, to minimise safety risk and maximise carbon gains. Please do not hesitate to contact me for further information Regards Henry Garcia On 24 Apr 2023, at 8:25 am, AgriProve wrote: Hi Henry, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of May 5th – June 5th? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions, please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Henry, Thanks for getting in touch. I have just completed your Annual Review so this is good timing. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project would not normally have met our threshold for resampling. However, as your project has reached the 5-year mark we will need to resample it ASAP. What we will do is - we will resample, and then to give us some more time to get the records together we will apply for a variation which will give us close to a year to get the records together. The records we need are: 1. Things showing that since starting the project in the past 5-6 years how stocking rate has changed- So this can be map's showing fencing you have done since starting the project, grazing records showing that you have changed the number of grazing days and rest ect. - these can be in any format that you have them in. We will take whatever you have even if its hand written and will ask questions or refine them if we need. Do you have those sorts of records? 1. For the emissions calculations - we need your fertilizer use from the 5 years of the project and the 5 years before the project started. This can simply be a list with what you have used each year e.g. 2020- Purchased 1 tonne of urea, 2022- XXXX going back 10 years. - our accountant documents can help you get an idea of this. 2. We also need estimated of your livestock numbers each year for the 5 years of the project and the 5 years before the project. People usually do this from their own records or as a starting point you can get your accountant to write out a document showing your livestock inventory over time. ( the 10 years) We need to know numbers and what they are e.g. lambs, calves, ewes, cows, bulls ect. I know this can seem like a lot but its simpler than it sounds and we will work with you to help you if you don't have great records. It would be great if you could start pulling some of this together, but like I said once we get the resampling done we have a bit of time. Are conditions suitable for us to come out and sample in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Due
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Andrew, Your carbon projects are currently due for their annual review. This has 2 parts. The first is a satellite assessment of your farms NDRE. This gives us an idea based on the vegetation change on your farm from satellite imagery whether carbon sequestration has been likely to occur. If this result is positive we will resample your projects to get a measurement and see if carbon sequestration has occurred. If it is negative- we will not resample and will reassess next year. The second part of this is we need to do a check-in to record what has been done, check in with you and make sure everything is going as planned. We are currently completing your satellite assessments and would love to get your check-in call done this week as well. Is there a time this week that suits you to go through this? It will take a maximum of 30 minutes and is generally a lot shorter than that. Could you please let me know a time that suits to call you or feel free to call me. Once this is done and we have all your results we can proceed with next steps. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Campbell Carbon Project 1 &  2
engagements.body: Good Morning Andrew, It has been 12 months since your carbon projects baseline sampling and therefore you are due for your first annual review. We do these each year to check you are on track and see if we think resampling would be worthwhile. This process has 2 parts, a satellite assessment and a check in call to tick of that you are meeting the requirements. I have just completed your satellite review and attached the results. This assessment uses NDRE (Normalized Difference Red Edge) to look at your vegetation changes overtime and we use it as an indicator of potential soil carbon sequestration. Your assessment has shown a positive change in the average NDRE from the baseline to the current period, which suggests resampling your projects this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration, this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Next steps are we need to do the check in call and confirm that you are happy for resampling to be completed in the next few weeks. Could you please confirm you are happy for us to resample and let me know a time that will work next week to go through the details. What day and time would be best to give you a call? engagements.subject: Frazer Carbon Project Review & Resampling Request
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Perina, I am getting in touch to update you with the next steps for your Carbon Project. I have just completed the desktop annual review of your project. This is where we assess the Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) change on your property overtime using satellite imagery. We use this as an indicator of potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. As you will see in the attached document there has not been a huge change over the period. Normally we would possibly not sample with a small change like this, however your project is in year 5 and re sampling is required to meet our reporting requirements. I will give you a call to discuss this, however if you haven't heard from me when you receive this email could you please get in touch asap to confirm next steps and resampling. I have attached a factsheet about the resampling process for your reference. If you have any questions feel free to reach out. engagements.body: Hi Bill, Yes, that looks to be better. Are you able to provide a short sentence or two on your farming experience? It will assist the regulator in their assessment. e.g. ‘I have been farming in the area for X years, with experience in regen/holistic grazing… any relevant education courses/university etc.’ Apologies I would try to get that out of Mel as I imagine she’s pretty familiar with your operation but she’s pre-occupied with other research tasks at the moment. I’ve gone ahead and mapped out the exclusions for the property, would you mind taking a look at the attached and letting me know if anything needs amending. Noting a couple of points: * I’ve removed the north-western portion of the title that looked to be crossing a fenceline to another paddock, and the northern section following the centre track up. Could you confirm those areas shouldn’t be included? * There appears to be some rocky outcrop areas that we may have difficulty sampling or achieving a minimum 30cm core. Areas like this should be excluded from the project if they can’t be consistently sampled. If you think we could sample those areas I can include them back in to the project. engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Your map is not right. I have been working on Google Maps , planning the 21 new paddocks, sheds, yards etc and I will get my son Will to send you the link so you can see. Contour banks are being removed and a couple of new laneways will be constructed to link all the paddocks. If you can get access to a current aerial image you will have a better idea of what is currently happening? You will have to leave the map with us for a bit longer before I can confirm the final location of the laneways. I have attached a PDF version of our Carbon Farming story so far. You might find something there of interest for the regulator. In my opinion the critical question that Agriprove should be asking potential carbon farmers is "A. Is your focus to make more MONEY or B. is your focus to make your soils more productive and resilient" ? There is a big difference. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used to measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The trend from the baseline to the current period indicates that NDRE has not shown a significant increase to meet our threshold for resampling this year (shown in the attached report). Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have gone over the last year for you on the property. I’ll attempt to contact you on your mobile in the coming days, but please feel free to reach me on 0408 448 190 at a time that suits you. QTR Check - 26/02/2025 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Please Cross check the eligible activities that were chosen by the landholder at the time of project registration are accurately captured against customer deal in HS: · Applying nutrients · Establishing and permanently maintaining pasture · Re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture · Altering the stocking rate 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 6 months? upgraded 1 pasture back into lucerne - trying to get 7-10 year cycle from it (doing 1 paddock a year) lime application (1-2 paddocks a year) targeting a pH of 6 in top 20cm - first time using a speedtiller this year 100-200kg single superphosphate each year Sheep - 1000 merino ewes lambing in june. send ewes off farm (agistment) end of dec-30 april and keep lambs on farm leave 10cm of groundcover 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 6 months? continue as they are - have already applied lime and rejuvenated 1 paddock with lucerne 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? spread lime on surface before project and now using a speedtiller to get it into the soil had previously been grazing down to bare dirt - now more aware and focused on keeping ground cover 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% paddock at a time 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} 2-3 weeks during lambing, they are spread out across the property to be set stocked until weaning 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} 21 months (dependent on rain) 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 15ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? hand written in farm diary - paddock plans 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? worthwhile keeping ground cover - not seeing the dirt fly away grass is more a more rain ready condition from keeping more ground cover 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? no 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? 2ha of trees last year 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? no

engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Morning Hamish, Thanks for getting this information back to me. I will get in touch with your bank manager in the next few weeks to get this moving. Your reporting deadline is not until August, so we do have a bit of time to tick everything off. In terms of the bank needing to give consent - we have to collect it as it's a requirement from the clean energy regulator. My understanding is they collect all eligible interest holder's consent as protection for the project by making sure everyone with an interest is aware of the project and acknowledges their intent to continue to meet its obligations. Eg. If someone involved with land didn't know about the project they may do something against the rules, people may try to sell their property and not mention it, people have tried to run projects without other owners knowing and some types of carbon projects require changes of practice which may impact your ability to pay the mortgage. Anything along those lines is why the bank needs to know. As far as I am aware we have never had a bank say no to us as a soil carbon is beneficial to your operation, It's more to make sure everyone is aware that needs to be, and they sign off on that. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Hamish I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not be positive - which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then, and we will have to complete a resampling at the 5-year mark. To tick off your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project and any key requirements for this year. Is there a time that suits you for me or someone from our team to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? engagements.subject: Re: Horizon
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Alec, Glad to hear you are excited about it. The areas that you see are based on the SOC model predictions, but also its relative within your farm. ( all measured from satellite predictions) So the best areas that are showing are the areas where the SOC model has had the most predicted change in soil carbon since your baseline period or had the most positive indicators present in those areas. It doesn't necessarily mean those areas have had an increase in carbon - its the best within your projects. For example: the people that have been in 3 years of drought and had barely any ground cover will still be seeing all 3 types of zones for their farms, its not showing where you are getting carbon and where you are not. We are planning to show specific predictions of carbon sequestered in the future, but we need to do a bit more testing on how accurate the predictions are before we are comfortable showing them in the platform. This model will be run every month ( see the timer in top right hand corner of the panel showing you when the next update will be ) and it will be updated in the platform automatically no matter the result. On our end if the model ran and predicted a worthwhile increase we are notified and would then look to resample even if it was out of your usual review time. This model allows us to check each month and act when a large enough increase is predicted instead of doing it once a year like we have in the past. IN the platform month to month you may not notice a huge difference as a month is not long in carbon time and therefore It you may take a while to see a large change in the areas that are in this current map layer. We are hoping to get some more time-based information and graphs in there in the future/ Hope you are well and if you have any more questions Im happy to chat. **Email**: 24 Apr 2026, 12:09 Subject: Re: Horizon From: Claudia Bryant To: matthewsalec244@gmail.com Hey Alec, No Worries. It's always good to check in case there is something wrong. Great to hear it's all going well! The HORIZON map is showing the carbon level change predictions for your farm. It uses all different layers and satellite imagery to get a prediction of what the carbon has done overtime. So the model does a prediction of how much carbon has increased or decreased across your farm since baseline (say for each 30m square) and then it groups it together to make the map you're seeing. So instead of you seeing all the little squares it smooths it out into areas to show you the lowest performing areas in orange, the areas that are within the average range in green and the highest performing areas in dark green. This makes it easier to action as it looks smoother and less complicated but does remove some of the finer details between areas in those zones. These are though just showing the relative areas on your farm- so where the best performance is in terms of carbon change is, it doesn't indicate if its an increase or decrease. So ultimately the model measures carbon change using satellite imagery. The current HORIZON map shows you your best performing areas, and the next step is for us to show the actual carbon predictions in the platform. It does this maths already we just aren't confident showing it publicly to everyone in the platform until we have done some more testing. Kind Regards, Claudia [Logged via email-to-HubSpot sync; Outlook Internet Message-ID: ]

This makes it easier to action as it looks smoother and less complicated but does remove some of the finer details between areas in those zones. These are though just showing the relative areas on your farm- so where the best performance is in terms of carbon change is, it doesn't indicate if its an increase or decrease e.g. a farm that's in drought and has had a decrease will still have all 3 colours and in that case the dark green would in theory show where they lost the least. ( it shows you the highest performing in terms of carbon but we don't currently indicate in platform if that is an increase or by how much). So ultimately the model measures carbon change using satellite imagery, The current HORIZON map shows you your best performing areas, and the next step is for us to show the actual carbon predictions in the platform. It does this maths already we just aren't confident showing it publicly to everyone in the platform until we have done some more testing and are confident that the predictions are accurate as the model is pretty new.) engagements.subject: AgriProve community meeting
engagements.body: Good morning Lisa, I hope you and your family are all well! AgriProve is excited to invite you and your husband to join us in Colosseum at Kylie and Lance Stephenson’s property for an AgriProve community event. A big thank you to Kylie and Lance for hosting the occasion! The event will be held on Wednesday 22nd of November at 1142 Blackmans Gap Road, Colosseum. Kick off will be at 10am, finishing at approximately 2pm. The days agenda: Morning Presentations: 10am – 12:00pm The morning will be a chance to learn about some of AgriProve’s new initiatives. Learn about the new opportunity to integrate cattle monitoring with your AgriProve soil carbon project and find out about the new reef credit opportunities upcoming through the Reef Credits: Grazing Land Management method, developed in partnership with Verterra and Greencollar. We are also excited to have a presentation from our keynote speaker, Mr Hobbs Magaret, coming all the way from the USA. Hobbs is a rancher from east Texas, founder of Sisters Cattle Co. and an expert in using ultra-high density grazing to maximise carbon drawdown and production efficiency. BBQ Lunch: 12:00 – 12:45 Following presentations there will be a chance to unwind with BBQ lunch and refreshments provided. Afternoon Farm Tour: 12:45 – 2:00pm To wrap up the day we will all head out for a farm tour led by Lance and Kylie to see what they are focusing on currently. It will also be an opportunity for everyone share stories about what has worked for them. If you are able to make it, we would love to see you there for what will be a great opportunity to meet others, share knowledge and a bite to eat. Please accept this invitation as soon as possible to RSVP. This will help us get an idea of numbers ahead of time. For any dietary requirements or if any family and friends would like to attend, we would love them to. Please simply notify us in advance at william@agriprove.io or team@agriprove.io. Kind regards, Team at AgriProve

engagements.subject: Carbon project Review Due
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Lisa, I am getting in touch as your carbon project is due for its Annual Review. This has 2 parts. The first is a satellite assessment of your farms NDRE. This gives us an idea based on the vegetation change on your farm from satellite imagery whether carbon sequestration has been likely to occur. If this result is positive, we will resample your project to get a measurement and see if carbon sequestration has occurred. If it is negative- we will not resample and will reassess next year. The other part of this is we need to do a check-in to record what has been done, check in with you and make sure everything is going as planned. We are currently completing your satellite assessments and would love to get your check-in call done this week as well. Is there a time this week that suits you to go through this? It will take a maximum of 30 minutes and is generally a lot shorter than that. Could you please let me know a time that suits to call you or feel free to call me. Once this is done and we have all your results we can proceed with next steps. I look forwarding to hearing from you. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve Platform
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Ian, Sorry it took a while for us to get back to you. I have just been passed your email asking about the AgriProve platform. See below in case you have forgotten. [cid:279333d1-f559-486e-8fae-45572d2540f2] To answer your questions: 1. Will the AgriProve platform do the same job as things like Agriwebb? At the moment No. Agri Webb has lots of farm management information and Features to help you run your farm. Our platform at the moment will focus on mainly things to help you with your projects and collecting info about carbon. Long term we may build things that integrate with it and have some overlap, but for now the main functionality of our platform is the scores, emissions calculator, we will be putting your soil sampling results in there and it is where you can use Ready Graze which is a software to use CERES Cattle tracking tags. For this reason to answer your second question - right now AgriWebb has better features for record keeping than our platform so it would be more suitable. However as long as you stay on top of your records for auditing you can store them however you like. 2. In terms of how we use the emissions calculations in the platform: These are purely to give you an idea of your emissions vs. what you are sequestering for your interest. We don't share this information or the result with anyone including the government. It is more an exercise to give you an idea of emissions vs. sequestration if you did want to pursue carbon neutrality, insetting ect. But to actually get the accreditation for those they have their own processes and measurements that would need to be done- The platform results would not be what they use and are not what we use in the crediting process either. I hope that helped! If you have any questions or want clarification feel free to give me a call. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Ian, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? Wednesday next week would be ideal, but happy to work around you.
