engagements.subject: AgriProve community event
engagements.body: Good morning Jim, I hope you and the family are well! AgriProve is excited to invite you to join us in Colosseum at Kylie and Lance Stephenson’s property for an AgriProve community event. A big thank you to Kylie and Lance for hosting the occasion! The event will be held on Wednesday 22nd of November at 1142 Blackmans Gap Road, Colosseum. Kick off will be at 10am, finishing at approximately 2pm. The days agenda: Morning Presentations: 10am – 12:00pm The morning will be a chance to learn about some of AgriProve’s new initiatives. Learn about the new opportunity to integrate cattle monitoring with your AgriProve soil carbon project and find out about the new reef credit opportunities upcoming through the Reef Credits: Grazing Land Management method, developed in partnership with Verterra and Greencollar. We are also excited to have a presentation from our keynote speaker, Mr Hobbs Magaret, coming all the way from the USA. Hobbs is a rancher from east Texas, founder of Sisters Cattle Co. and an expert in using ultra-high density grazing to maximise carbon drawdown and production efficiency. BBQ Lunch: 12:00 – 12:45 Following presentations there will be a chance to unwind with BBQ lunch and refreshments provided. Afternoon Farm Tour: 12:45 – 2:00pm To wrap up the day we will all head out for a farm tour led by Lance and Kylie to see what they are focusing on currently. It will also be an opportunity for everyone share stories about what has worked for them. If you are able to make it, we would love to see you there for what will be a great opportunity to meet others, share knowledge and a bite to eat. Please accept this invitation as soon as possible to RSVP. This will help us get an idea of numbers ahead of time. For any dietary requirements or if any family and friends would like to attend, we would love them to. Please simply notify us in advance at william@agriprove.io or team@agriprove.io. Kind regards, Team at AgriProve

engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Irvine and Wynne Carbon Projects
engagements.body: Hi Jim, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your projects. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have been going on the ground of your project, one of our team will attempt to contact you in the coming days on your mobile. On this call we will confirm that you are happy to go ahead with re-sampling your project. Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. engagements.subject: AgriProve EIH Consent
engagements.body: Hi Jim, One of the key components for project compliance and ACCU issuance is the requirement of all Eligible Interest Holders (EIH) to consent to Registering a project with the Emissions Reduction Fund. We would like to commence this Eligible Interest Holder consent process, as your projects are about to progress through to the T2 sampling round. Should this sampling round measure an increase, we will require this EIH process to be completed to fulfil the compliance obligations on your project. The consent forms attached are required to be signed by all parties with “Eligible Interest” as per the land title(s) on which the project is Registered. According to the titles registered there are three eligible interest holders that require consent: Christine Wieland as the sole director of JCBL Pty Ltd - listed on 46/RP893332 Christine Wieland as owner of 162/CPFL40130, 4/CPFL40130, 8/SP120836, 67/CPFD137 National Australia Bank Limited bank manager as mortgage holder of 46/RP893332 Could you please sign and return your EIH Consent form as soon as possible and speak with your Bank manager about obtaining their signature. If your bank manager has any questions, please feel free to pass along the contact details for your project owner, Joanne Curran (joanne@agriprove.io). I have also CC'd her on this email for reference. A couple of points for your bank manager that may assist in their processes: You have had a lead indicator assessment on your carbon project that shows a possibility of a measured increase in SOC, which may proceed through to an offsets report submission for an ACCU claim. The operation of the soil carbon project does not involve any land use change and is focused on improved agricultural management to ultimately sequester carbon in soil. Regulatory risks related to project operation are covered by AgriProve as project proponent (as per AgriProve agreements). Thanks for your assistance in getting this signed and doing this as soon as possible. This should not hold up the offsets report or audit process, however if it is not completed it will delay any issuance of ACCUs. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Wynne/Irvine Carbon Projects Update
engagements.body: Hi Jim, Just the public holiday in Qld today. Regarding the Irvine project, and given that we have not yet measured an increase in soil carbon, the decision to continue the project comes down to the expected benefit from any ongoing management. The outlays for management improvements you’ve made are already in place, so the only cost of staying in is time, and the upside is retaining the option on future ACCUs from a property where the eligible activities are already established. Exiting now permanently closes that door. It’s also worthwhile thinking about whether the carbon levels measured at the point of baselining (Jan 2021) were abnormally high from back-to-back good seasons prior, and what climate conditions have been like relatively speaking in the years since. Did the bushfire and flood also affect this property? We’d want to rule out those as possible factors to explain the decrease in carbon first. Could you please provide more information on the timing of your keylining and pondage banking on the property? This may have had a larger than anticipated initial effect on water retention and sequestration potential. From our side, consideration would also be given to the costs of auditing the project, but the decision to continue is ultimately yours. Your reading of the EIH is broadly correct, rescinding a project is possible and is much simpler if no ACCUs have been issued. You would essentially not be bound to the permanence obligations to maintain any sequestered carbon. Regarding planned tillage on the Wynne project, this is perfectly fine and allowed under the Methodology, but should be done in a way that minimises soil disturbance and exposure/volatilisation to the atmosphere, i.e. timing to align with forecast rains and reinstating of soils as soon as possible. Depth of tillage must also be limited to no greater that 90cm below ground level if deep till/ripping is involved. There may be a short-term dip in carbon levels, so we’d want a reasonable establishment period after sowing before the next sampling event. Hopefully that helps, and more than happy to discuss anything further over the phone. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Blewett & Jones Carbon Projects - Annual Review
AgriProve - Regarding the Beef Herd Methodology Suspension

engagements.body: QTR Check - 14/01/2025 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting Jones CPs Altering the stocking rate Blewett CPs Altering the stocking rate Establishing, and permanently maintaining, a pasture where there was previously no or limited pasture, such as on cropland or fallow 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? Jones (Sunnyholt) - Maintained rotational grazing system, feed licks with legume seeds. Using the Optiweigh system to measure stock in the paddock, total/average/minimum herd weights. Focusing on legume establishment and rotational grazing. CP2 and CP8 have had good establishment with a seed spreader. Blewett (Tullumun) - Big push to improve fencing to be stock proof, now 90% complete. New rotational grazing system in place, installed 9 troughs, feed licks with legume seeds to help spread it out on the paddocks. Exclusion fencing to keep kangaroos off the property, ongoing. Damage mitigation permit to remove kangaroos with parks and wildlife, culling up to 1,000. CP1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 - cattle taken off and allowed to rest. plan is to spread legumes slowly and let native grasses grow back. Have maintained 2 paddocks as a grass pasture CP2 and CP8 - previously cultivation paddocks (oats on CP2 and sorghum, oats and wheat on CP8) converted to bambatsi grass, and seeding Buffel grass as a short-term solution to kangaroo control. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Jones - Continue managing the herds in a rotational system. Blewett - Plan is to spread legumes slowly and let native grasses grow back. Continue rotational grazing. 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Jones - Materially Different. Had Leucaena already established, but now going down the progardes route (smaller plant that requires zero maintenance). Using Optiweigh and Pheonix mapping app, allows them to take better records of stock movements and potentially replace the grazing calendar. Now using an excel program to judge how long to leave cattle in paddock, grass budget now conducted every winter, calculates feed budgets and a more even graze across the whole property. Adjust stock numbers accordingly based on available feed budget. Blewett - New. Property was very run down when purchased in 2020. Not using Optiweigh, but have implemented the rotational grazing system. 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% Jones - New grazing system 100%. Projects 4, 7 and 9 are well established already with legumes. Blewett - 100% for rotational grazing. Not obvious where legumes are at present, have put feed licks out on every project but yet to see them establish. 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} Jones - around 40 days Blewett - around 30 days in each project 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} Jones - 150 days Blewett - 230 days 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} Jones - 100 ha Blewett - 200 ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? Pheonix mapping app, combined with an excel spreadsheet to track feed budgeting and stock movement. RCS grazing charts up to this point, but moving towards the above digital approach. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? Jones - Harder to observe the difference as rotational system already in place. Selling a lot of feeders in the last 12 months. Definitely have seen an improved diversity of grass species. Blewett - bigger changes observed, soil health (grasses) and pastures darker green,…

engagements.body: Hi Maddie, Please see agenda attached for the site visits. We are proposing to stay in Arcadia Valley on Monday 30th June, complete Jones CP 1-9 audit site visits on Tuesday 1st of July. We will then drive to Blewett site on Wednesday 2nd July and complete half of site visits, and complete the rest on Thursday 3rd of July in AM. I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. The main aspects that will be discussed are specified below: 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of dates provided in your farm management record) 2. Detailed description of all land management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA (as per the farm management record) 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points. Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically farm house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the farm, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to farm house/office - informal interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that farm records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the farm records (such as livestock, invoices for inputs, contracts or invoices relating to management activities * Confirmation that we (yourself and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the Carbon project operation, implementation and administration Accommodation would be great, thank you. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Rowan and Maddie, I have just completed our annual satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, some of your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the baseline period. This indicates a trend in the vegetation that suggests carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in those areas and we will potentially resample your projects this year. If we do resample, we will focus on the ones that have had a positive result in this review. Those being Jones projects 2,3,4,5,7,8,9 and we will reassess the Blewett projects and those within Jones that were negative again next year. From here we will put your projects through the model to determine if that backs up this indicator, have a look at our sampling schedule to see if we have some others in the area we can fit in with yours and do our check in call to determine if and when we will resample. Is there a time that suits you for me or someone from our team to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Jones and Blewett CPs
engagements.body: Dear Rowan and Maddie, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. From: Alan Rissmann Sent: Monday, July 29, 2024 3:30 PM To: Imogen Hickey Subject: Re: Soil re-sampling results by strata G'day Imogen Is it possible to grab the SAR test results in excel form please? Thanks Alan On Thu, Jan 4, 2024 at 11:28 AM Imogen Hickey > wrote: Hi Alan, Apologies for the delayed response. We have broken down the SOC change by strata in the tables below. A key point to consider when looking at these results is that there is potentially a higher variability/volatility with the results due to the strata being based on paddocks rather than stratification based on variability in the soil. Stratification that is based on soil variables such as elevation, K-Gamma or clay content is targeted to reduce soil carbon variability and will also reflect the response within the strata to management activities. We might consider re-stratification at the next sampling round to reduce this variability. Another reason why some of the strata could have particularly low results is that some of the sample points have landed on the edge of the paddock/fence line, such as CEA1-S4 and CEA2-S3 for Rosedale CP, which could be dragging the average down as there are only three samples within each strata. The sample point locations are randomly generated which means that we cannot control where the sample points are located. However this could just provide an explanation for results that are particularly low when considering the different crops and applications applied to the paddocks/strata and the impact on soil carbon. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Lynch Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Derek, Thank you for your patience with us completing your annual review. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the previous period to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I am working on the other items that we discussed on Friday regarding T0-T1 results and an overlay of your paddocks with the carbon project boundaries. As always if you have any questions, feel free to reach out to any of the team. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Derek, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not be positive comparatively - which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year or when our HORIZON model is fully up and running to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. if you have any questions or would like to touch base about your carbon project- feel free to call me anytime. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lynch CP
engagements.body: Dear Derek, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.body: Hi Dylan I recognise things look pretty grim with those results. When we bought the property in 2020 a large part of the property has a neglected vineyard that was full of weeds. That and the fact the region was coming out of drought end 2019 meant that the carbon was building but the land was unusable. In 2021 we pulled out the old vineyard and began a program to move to ½ perennial and ½ seasonal pasture. Efforts were hampered due to repeated flooding, consequential land and infrastructure damage and budget limitations. Things seem to have stabilised now (fingers crossed). We got a good paddock of oats out this year and have done a lot to control the weeds. We're planning to start turning one section (about 8 ha) to perennial pasture. Would you suggest that is now not a possibility? Are we able to choose a time of the year that better aligns with seasonal conditions from your perspective? engagements.subject: Staples Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Charlotte, Thank you for your time on the phone just now. We have completed the annual review of your Staples Carbon Project as part of our project monitoring process. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used to measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The trend from the baseline to the current period indicates that NDRE has not shown a significant increase to meet our threshold for resampling this year (shown in the attached report). Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Charlotte, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do this every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This result means that carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred, and your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year and when our HORIZON model is fully up and running to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? engagements.subject: Interview for Carbon Builders
engagements.body: Hi John, Thank you again for your time on the phone yesterday. I have written up a draft of piece that we would like to share with the AgriProve Carbon Builders Facebook group, I will pop it below in this email. Please have a look over it and send back any concerns or thoughts with the information included. We are happy to alter and change things if you are not comfortable sharing certain pieces of information. Here is the draft: "Good afternoon, Carbon Builders! This week we have an insight to another one of our members, John Monaghan from Rocking Chair Farm in the Hunter region, NSW. John discussed his farm management and soil carbon results in an interview below. Bio and carbon project: John and his business partner Alan Smith run a cattle and sheep grazing operation near Dungog, NSW, and have been involved in a carbon project since 2020. They had wanted to transition to regenerative agriculture to build their soil carbon levels; however, the financial input to develop the property to include more paddocks, water points and shade were large. These implementation costs were a main motivator for starting a carbon project. The financial benefits from increasing carbon levels helped incentivise the change in management. Previous Management: Prior to starting a carbon project, John was running 45 cow calves with minimal rotation through the 7 paddocks on Rocking Chair Farm. Annuals and perennials were direct drilled into a portion of the property and assisted by fertilisers, herbicides and insecticides. engagements.body: Hi John, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. engagements.subject: McLachlan CP - Soil Sampling Results
engagements.body: Hi John, Thank you for your recent assistance with organising the resampling of your soil carbon project. The results from the sampling indicated that your soil carbon levels have increased enough to warrant progressing to reporting and crediting. Well done on this achievement, it is very exciting news and a great result! While this is a significant step towards achieving credits, further reporting and calculations are required before we can provide an indication of the number of credits that will be awarded. The first step is for us to clarify any increases to your emissions as a result of operating your project. Any emissions associated with the implementation of your project must be accounted for to enable calculation of the net project impact. To help us be as organised as possible in this stage of the process I would like to organise a Crediting Kick-Off meeting. If you could let me know a time that would be convenient for you, I can send out a meeting invite. In the meeting we will cover the following: * Review of sampling results for McLachlan CP * Workflow for crediting * Review emissions reporting * Review of next immediate steps Kind regards, Imogen Hickey | Crediting Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 46 7645 Mobile: +61 402 509 303 Email: imogen@agriprove.io Address: [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DC99D2.1D71A040] [cid:image004.png@01DC99D2.1D71A040] [cid:image005.png@01DC99D2.1D71A040] [cid:image006.png@01DC99D2.1D71A040] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: HI Mitch, No Worries. I will check in with Geoff about where Beale and Cooper are up to. The most recent result for Watson was positive, and we are planning to resample. You should hear from Will soon about logistics with that soon. For the NDRE: All we get is what we send you with the line ( attached in case you didn't see the recent email I sent). We are working on building some NDRE and making it a bit more useful into the platform at the moment, but it is a little while away from being more than that line for now. We did run the project through the HORIZON model, and things are looking very promising. The output it gives at the moment is not very friendly to send or view. Its basically a lot of numbers, it requires a lot of interpretation and it is still a prototype, so we aren't going to share the results until we have calibrated it a bit more. It has suggested though that it is very likely that you have had an increase significant enough to be credited a second time around. From next week you will be able to see some of the HORIZON information in the platform - it will show you zones of your best performing, average, and lower performing areas in terms of carbon sequestration. This will be interesting to see what's happening across the area and in future will be able to give you carbon predictions. Would love your feedback on that once it is up and running. From: Will Frecheville Sent: Friday, March 8, 2024 9:53 AM To: Peter Ramsey Cc: Angus and Emily, Peter and Julie Ramsey Subject: RE: Farm Management Records - Lyne CP Hi Peter, Thanks for the call - please see attached with correction for the landholder statement page (apologies for the spelling mistake) and have also added in Angus and Emily as well, just for completeness. All you need to do is print out the statement page, sign, and re-send, and I will compile the complete document, and send to you for your records. As discussed, these records will from the basis of every crediting application going forward, but now that we've got all the baseline records sorted, for future, all we need is the updated changes as they occur. The threshold is simple for your project, in that the change in complete uncontrolled grazing, to a controlled grazing approach is an eligible activity which will be continually implemented in all reporting periods going forwards. The evidence for this, is as simple as a plan for goat/cattle movement, and that you've upgraded fencing (compared to the baseline); which is easy to prove. Lastly, as mentioned, one of my colleagues Jo will get in touch about updating the contract/sales agreement to include Angus and Emily as landholders and operators of the project. She will be able to answer any further questions relating to the agreement, it should be as simple as an amendment to have Angus and Emily included, with no changes to the overall agreement. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Process changes impacting projects registered after 8th November
engagements.body: Dear Tony, Yolande, Fred and Rita, I hope this message finds you well. Since our conversation and decision to execute the documentation for the additional projects in the pipeline for Corally Glen, there has been some development with the regulator that I wanted to pass on to keep you informed. The importance of the update is that it may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. I understand the additional document has only just come through, so I apologies about the quick turn around, but I wanted to do you the curtesy of providing you as much time as possible. As it turns out, the decision to proceed with registration now, but hold off baselining was made at a fortuitous time to avoid this additional paperwork! Please note that as discussed, signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately. Your projects can be withdrawn up until point of baseline and we will work with you to schedule sampling if you would like to proceed, and at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. You will also notice the quote came to $13,000 for the additional projects, not the expected $17,000 which is fantastic. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. I'll give you a call tomorrow to make sure you received my email and should you have any questions or need assistance, don’t hesitate to reach out. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note this is not a bad thing or indicative of if things are going backwards, it just means that there hasn't been enough positive change yet to justify resampling, which is to be expected as your project is not even 12 months old. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: Carbon Prediction Report
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, Thanks for your time on the phone this morning. I have attached a HORIZON report for you to show your neighbour. These are what we make up for people when they are interested in a project , so if he is interested, he can get in touch with us and we will do one up for him. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note this is not a bad thing or indicative of if things are going backwards, it just means that there hasn't been enough positive change yet to justify resampling, which is to be expected as your project is not even 12 months old. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: AgriProve project requirments
engagements.body: Hi Tony, Thank you for your time today. Following our conversation this morning, we have chased a few different scenarios that we thought might work better for you and come back with a feasible alternative. We have spoken with Hone and got approval for a smaller project area with increased sampling density for Double Valley. This would allow us to keep the double valley project on only the land titles you own, while still satisfying grant requirements. This will save Darren and Jacqueline needing to be involved and avoid any potential sale of property complication on their block. If you are happy with this new structure, the Double Valley projects eligible hectares should come to about 260Ha, with 32 cores in total. This will be confirmed once re-mapped. To help us progress, can you please: Confirm if you are happy with the new structure, or whether would like to proceed with including part of your parents block. Mark up the areas you would like taken out of project for Corally Glen to bring down baseline sampling. I have provided two images of the property below for this. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note this is not a bad thing or indicative of if things are going backwards, it just means that there hasn't been enough positive change yet to justify resampling, which is to be expected as your project is not even 12 months old. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Fred and Rita, Next week at the conference, AgriProve will be running a session (Wednesday 5th Nov) called: Project Ecosystem in Action: The Carbon Farming Value Chain It’s a practical look at how the different parts of the soil carbon value chain work together - from the producer and input suppliers to the technology side and the market. The idea is to show what’s actually happening on the ground and how soil carbon projects turn into real outcomes for producers and the broader market. If you’re coming along, it’d be great to see you there or have a chat at the stand afterwards. All the best, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io On Sunday, 19 October 2025, 9:44:03 am +1100, Claudia Bryant wrote: Hi Fred and Rita, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. Here’s the link if you’d like to check out the program: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/ Hope to see you there, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io

engagements.subject: Re: Carr Carbon Project - HORIZON Snapshot
engagements.body: HI Tony, Yes, that is the whole area. Carr projects 1,2,3 and 4. Map attached. Did not all of these projects go ahead? (the number of 3 projects in the report that is based on what we would have put that area into now if you were starting a project now - which is what these reports are designed for) In the Report- See that value that says estimated ACCU's/ha/year of 3.5 ACCU's/ha/year. That is basically saying this area that is the expected return. So if the area is 300ha then you times it by 3.5 to get the estimate per year- then times that number by 25 to get the total result for the 25 years of the project. We can make you up a more specific report, but I need more detail on what exactly that area is your looking at because we store it by project info and land titles not property names. QTR Check - XX/XX/2024 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Please Cross check the eligible activities that were chosen by the landholder at the time of project registration are accurately captured against customer deal in HS: · Re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture Could consider changing the stocking rate as a new activity - hot wiring and subdivision of paddocks is new since the project started (same with Findley CP). 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? Have fully renovated approx. 75% of paddocks, one paddock has been broadcast with multi species rather than renovated. Bottom right corner paddock has had seed creep from neighbouring paddock, not directly resown. Seeding once a year in Autumn. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Will continue the practice in the years to come. 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Yes, new. Not conducted in the baseline period. 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% 75% of paddocks resown to date 100% of property has had altered grazing management 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} Aim for 1 day in strong growing seasons, up to a week over winter. This property is just for finishing. 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} Average is close to 100 days, can stretch out to 150 days. Wouldn't ever go below 40 days. 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 1ha at most. 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? Agriwebb, spreadsheets. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? Yes, better response rate to rain events, better weight gain in animals. Ability to hold ground cover through dry periods, animals have improved health through the multispecies. 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? None. 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? None 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? This discussion has been helpful to understand the restrictions on the project and more consistent communication.

engagements.subject: Call with Pippa Mills - Findley CP
engagements.body: Annual Review Implementation Call May 2025 Have they been informed of and seen their LIA results? Yes Notes: Frazer CP has been sent, however we identified that we should also do a review at this time of year for Findley CP as well- they are both coming up for 5 year review this year. I will do that after this call and let her know the outcome for this second project. Have they been informed of the next steps and timeline for resampling? Yes Notes: Plan is to be resampled due to 5 year timeline for both projects. Operations will be in touch to confirm logistics and other things needed for 5 year review. What did you do in the project areas in the past year? and when? Notes: They have renovated pasture as planned, they sow on autumn rain due to it having reliable rainfall each year, it has been a little bit later than normal ( just had) but have sown and renovated pasture as intended. They cant do it all at once as they need to do it slowly so they have feed while the other areas are establishing. They have planted multispecies pasture and renovated 18 ha of pasture this year. They have also improved their grazing management regularly overtime. Did everything go as planned and you got what you wanted to done? Yes Notes: Everything is going as planned. Ask if and where they did each of the activities listed? and what percentage estimates of the areas? 5. For each of the eligible activities described above, please describe over what area these activities have been completed on a per project basis. For example: Project Name/Number: Eligible Activity: Implemented area %: Notes: Last year in the review they had completed 50% of the village lane property project (Frazer CP) , and 45% on the project that runs across 2 properties ( Findley CP) . They have now completed an additional 15% on each bringing the total renovated pastures in the project areas to 65% and 55%. They have improved their grazing on 100% of the area overtime. Did you have any fires, droughts, floods ect. - If so in what project areas.4. Have there been any changes or unforeseen events that impact your carbon project areas since the start of your project (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings, land sale, bushfire, flood)? - word better and be mre sepcific. no Notes: They did complete tree plantings last year and it was noted/recorded in last years annual review. (Landholder told me this). Did you apply any fertiliser, seed or proudcts to the areas? get names, species, dates, rates and specific locations of each Notes: They have completely changed to a blanket rule of no synthetic fertilizers. They have used Nutrisoil and Soluphos on the pasture once they have leaves, it is a foliar applicant. How do you graze those areas differently to what you did before? what were you doing then and what about now? could ask about fencing, stocking rates ect. Notes: They have changed how they graze - increasing there grazing intervals. Meaning how many days between grazes each paddock gets. Originally it was 30 days between grazes of the paddock - aka 30 days rest --> and now it is between 60 and 100 days depending on weather. They have also shortened the period of time that is spent in each paddock. They have done this by temporary fencing to change paddock sizes, they have sacrifice areas where they hold animals to feed them to allow the paddocks to still be rested at key times ( giving more days rest) and They are adjusting their production system and stocking numbers eg. instead of fattening all the steers they breed for 2 years every year, they will keep heifers and lower the numbers of steers depending on available feed and season. The example they used is they used to fatten alot (100-200 steers) and now they mostly do around 40. (check this with them in future if specifics are needed.) They are also feeding breeders hay sometimes to free up feed for animals they are fattening to put less pressure on pasture and still achieve production goals. 8. If altering the…

engagements.subject: Grazing Management Changes and Timeline
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Thanks for your time just before, as discussed, the CER has asked about the grazing practice changes you have made. Specifically, the first water upgrades in 2021, and some sub-divisions of paddocks. We need to show a clear timeline of additional fencing upgrades/changes post the April 2022 declaration, as well as changes to stocking rates/durations of grazing following the seeding and application of Rural Boss. When we were on site, I remember you saying you're constantly making changes, based on behaviours to optimise the approach and your grazing management, so I do not think we will have an issue showing this change. As a first step, whilst you're putting together some timelines against your notes, can you please send me some photos of your grazing charts (as many years back as you have) We did have an option to not have grazing included as an eligible activity, however given it is central to your operation, I do not want to let this eligible activity go. engagements.subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. From: Jeff Bell Sent: Sunday, 2 February 2025 2:55 PM To: Dylan Jones Subject: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Dylan, The Agriprove platform said "Generate income through a Reef Credit project Your property is eligible to undertake a Reef Credit Project." Is this correct or is it just that we are geographically eligible? Can a reef credit project co-exist with a carbon project? I have been looking into "natural sequence farming" which is all about keeping water and dissolved nutrients on farm through modifying existing contour drains and/or constructing level contours.(which fits neatly into what the "reef credit project" would be looking to achieve. Attended a "natural sequence farming" field day yesterday and there was so much that explained why areas of our farm have limited performance compared to the mean. If we spend money on training and earthworks to keep more water and nutrients on our farm(approx 94 % of which is under a carbon project) would we be eligible for a "reef credit project"? Jeff Bell

engagements.subject: Re: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Definitely would not be grazing management as that is already done. It would be remedial earth works to modify the existing drain contours and where needed construct new contours to slow the flow of water and nutrients and keep both on farm rather than running off down the waterway which does come in the list of gully management methodology activities. Most of the farm can benefit from this in productivity(and consequently carbon sequestration) but only about 30 percent of the farm(my guestimate) has substandard ground cover which in my opinion could release some sediment and nutrients off farm. My take is that the amount of sediment lost from the farm in its current condition would be to low to bother with. The only place where there would be any amount would be a bit hard to manage as it comes pouring through from next door in a water way only a couple of hundred metres from our bottom fence. If Agriprove think there is anything worth pursuing then I will think about it. I myself think not but that is an opinion not based on knowledge. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jeff, I have just completed your yearly satellite assessment for your carbon project. As you know we use this as an indicator for if we think resampling would be worthwhile. Your assessment this year ( attached) has shown an increase in the average NDRE from baseline to current period and an increase in the past year. This indicates that re-sampling this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration. This does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We need to complete the physical sampling to know what is happening in the ground. Next steps: Before we schedule the resampling date, we need to complete the phone call section of the review. Is there a time next week that would suit to do that? I have some prep I need to do before the call so locking in a time in advance works best. If you have any questions please let me know. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Re: Soil testing extras?
engagements.body: Good Moring Jeff, Yeah it is completely possible for us to do that. Do you know exactly what tests you want done? For an idea of potential price and difference tests I have attached an example of a quote we got for someone else and the full price list. Keeping in mind this is an older one and they may have changed since then. I had a look at your project, and you have 9 sample sites. You would see that on your results in the past you have 18 because they test the top layer (0-30cm) and then a deeper piece of that sample ( 30-100cm). If you wanted to do both depths, you would need to pay for 18 samples. ( 2x 9) Dylan did mention though that generally for agronomic based things having the deeper samples may not give you a lot of value but that depends on what you want to look at. Let me know what you're thinking and we can go from there. engagements.body: Thanks Claudia, but I won’t be travelling to Albury. Fairly happy with things but would be ecstatic if we could get under a storm. Currently broad casting 18 species of seed in front of moves of our current steer intake. Using temporary fencing and a batlatch this year to increase the impact on seeded paddocks. If we ever do get some rain I have some extra ingredients to go into our bio stimulant and some changes of ratios and also have added some biochar into our cattle’s diet courtesy of some presentations and schooling I was fortunate enough to attend this year. Graham Sait for one day, Christine Jones on another day(plus some one on one next day at another farm and then a 3 day school with Nicole Masters. A bit of information overload in a fairly short space of time but a lot of value. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. WH William Hyem 19 Jun, 23 Hi Geoff, Please see the attached results for Cooper and Beale soil carbon projects. When the results were returned in June, we did find that some of the samples did not reach the full 30cm depth requirement for the methodology, and so we are likely going to need to resample and potentially re-stratify based on what is known of the area. Also, please find in three separate follow up emails the forwarded Sales and Licence Agreements for all projects, originally sent to gbfox@nidebra.com in December 2021. We have updated our Sales and Licence Agreement since then, so if you have received legal advice on the attached and are happy to sign that’s great – if you have not yet received legal advice please let me know and I will get you a single SLA on the updated terms. The terms are mostly the same, there have been some additions for data management and also non-performance clauses to remove AgriProve as project proponent under certain conditions as well which gives a bit more flexibility. I have attached the terms of the new agreement for your reference. Finally, with regards to invoicing the baseline sampling quote in an email 14/12/2021 was Beale: $4,000 ex. GST upfront and Cooper: $6,000 ex. GST upfront, or $12.50 ACCU forward abatement loan (let me know if you want to discuss this option, I believe last we spoke payment upfront was your preference). There was also the extra cost for agricultural analytes which were sent to yourself and Mitch last year. We have discussed the invoice for Watson Carbon Project previously and we cannot find record in xero or transaction history that this has been paid (original invoice attached). If you have paid this, would you please be able to send through remittance of the transaction? Thank you for your patience, sorry I know we have a bit to work through here but give me a call to discuss as ever on 0456 312 603. Kate MS Mat Silver 18 May, 22 Email sent regarding project support - see Cooper CP notes for a copy. KC Kate Carmichael 30 Sep, 21 RFI on CTR-CTI, needs one more director signature

engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: Sampling Results - Nox 2024
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Please see attached the results from the last round of sampling completed on the two project areas. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting. From: Ross Thompson Sent: Saturday, 7 June 2025 1:03 PM To: Kieren Whittock Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Kieren, I was wondering if it is possible that we could delay catching up on this until mid Spring? I feel you will have more chance of "cutting through" with me then, when I start heading into our slower time of year (Mid Spring til late Summer). As you know, I am pretty wound up with the CER and their demands and then the fact that "estimates" are OK. I just do not see how I can possibly justify loading up future generations with this burden. But I think, given all the work we have done up til now, I should listen carefully to you, and we should TRY to resolve it and move on. Rather than throwing the baby out with the bath water. No promises that you will be able to swing me around in my attitude. But if you can wait until I am more receptive, I think it gives us the best chance. What are your thoughts? If you are agreeable, have diarised to get in touch with you by email on October 1. I would simply be replying to your email below to get the ball rolling and set aside some time for us to work on it together as you suggested. Regards Ross From: Kieren Whittock > Sent: Friday, 28 March 2025 9:46 PM To: Ross Thompson > Subject: RE: Agriprove form for the CER Hi Ross, So having a look in some more detail here. As discussed we are trying to achieve two things with this information. 1. Show that at least one of the eligible activities has been implemented on the project area 2. Gather the data we need to quantify emissions associated with the project that feed into the calculations Regarding point 1, this is what we are trying to achieve with the Activity Log pages. What is important to note on these activities is that we only need to demonstrate that one of these has occurred, not all of them. As a starting point we could select one that may be the easiest to demonstrate, and only make reference to the others as complimentary activities without being required to demonstrate them in detail or provide detail that is difficult to obtain. From your notes it sounds like this may be achievable. Regarding point 2, if we put aside the stock numbers for the moment, we can strike a few things out from the start. I don't believe irrigation and landscape modification are relevant in your scenario and can be disregarded. That leaves the inputs, which it seems you have some records for, at least for total quantities which we will be able to work with. I also think residues will be able to be resolved given you are primarily a grazing operation and this section is more aimed at cropping operations. Regarding stock numbers, I think it would be worthwhile if we could jump on a quick call with Will at a time that suits you to ask some targeted questions that can help us better determine what can be done. Also, to clarify, the expectation is not for you to fill out the tables provided - we can do this work based on raw information provided, before cross-checking with you that we have interpreted correctly. As discussed, I would be more than happy to come and see you face to face, I could complete as much of this as I can on the fly while there - we have done this a few times previously and has b…

engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Morning Ross, Thanks for sending those details through. We definitely haven't put it in the too hard basket - it just hasn't been an urgent priority up until now as it's coming up to the reporting period date. I will touch base with Kieren and have cc'ed him into this email to see what we can do. In terms of the record keeping - we would never expect you to guess, and it is a lot simpler than it sounds. Most of it is things that you would already have had to collect and would have given to your accountant eg. invoices for expenses such as seed and fertilizer, livestock numbers, fuel used ect. The main thing that the regulator needs is proof that you have changed practices in some way and that you have implemented what you said you would. They don't need extreme detail of every little thing that you have done on farm. If you would find it helpful, I can jump on a call with you and we can look at your map, go through what you've done on your project, what records you have, and put together a bit of a plan/list of what you need to proceed and get this done. engagements.subject: Call with Ross Thompson
engagements.body: Outbound answered call via Dylan Jones made by Dylan Jones - Call back Ross Thompson +61439179269 Call ID: 3770419144 Chifley Carbon Project — Call Summary Parties: Dylan Jones (AgriProve) & Ross Thompson (landholder) Paddock Configuration Paddock layout has changed since baseline — new fence lines were added in 2021–22 , marked on a sketch map Ross sent through during the call. Eligible Activity — Pasture Rejuvenation (Paddock J4A) Paddock J4A is the only paddock where additional work was carried out. It was cropped for three years (zero-till) , then zero-till pasture was re-established. This occurred last year (i.e. FY2024–25), not FY22–23 as previously recorded — Ross confirmed the earlier record was incorrect. Ross noted he hadn't included it in records due to its small size, but Dylan confirmed it should be documented regardless. Eligible Activity — Grazing Management (Main Activity) Start date confirmed: 01/01/2022. Ross linked this to a significant bull sale in September 2021, after which capital works and intensified grazing management commenced. Dylan had initially suggested 07/01/2021 but Ross preferred 01/01/2022 as more accurate. Declaration date on file: April 2021. Stocking Rate / Grazing Practice Changes Ross does not manage to a specific LSU or head-per-paddock target. His grazing targets are: Maintain pasture sward at 10 cm minimum at all times Target 100% ground cover Average grazing duration per paddock: ~1 week (5–10 days) Previously, stock were set-stocked for up to 6 weeks — a significant change in grazing intensity/duration At any one time, approximately 90% of the property is rested Next Steps Dylan to finalise the landholder statement document and send to Ross for review Ross to sign page 3 (landholder statement page) Following sign-off, move to audit engagement

engagements.subject: Sampling Results - Nox 2024
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Please see attached the results from the last round of sampling completed on the two project areas. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting. Regards, Kieren Whittock | National Operations Manager [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 467 645) Mobile: +61 400 216 548 Email: kieren@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DB8910.0A084DC0] [cid:image004.png@01DB8910.0A084DC0] [cid:image005.png@01DB8910.0A084DC0] [cid:image006.png@01DB8910.0A084DC0] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. In summary: * Chifley Carbon Project is now 650 tC above the baseline carbon stock and has shown a consistent increasing trend since the sampling round completed in early 2023. This means we can go ahead and begin the process of reporting and applying for ACCUs for this project. * Daly Carbon Project is not above the baseline carbon stock to date however this project shows the same consistent increasing trend since the early 2023 sampling, with three of the 4 CEAs continuing to show gains since 2023. Overall I think these are really positive results. With regard to Chifley Carbon Project, before we can estimate the total ACCU yield we will need to do some work to estimate any emissions associated with the project period to feed into our calculations. I have copied Imogen Hickey to this email who is our crediting specialist, it would be great if we can arrange a time to jump on a video call to talk through the process from here and next steps to work toward lodging an application for ACCUs. Feel free to give me a call or otherwise let us know a time that might suit for a brief meeting. engagements.body: Hi Ross, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Ross, Next week at the conference, AgriProve will be running a session (Wednesday 5th Nov) called: Project Ecosystem in Action: The Carbon Farming Value Chain It’s a practical look at how the different parts of the soil carbon value chain work together - from the producer and input suppliers to the technology side and the market.
