engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Morning Ross, Thanks for sending those details through. We definitely haven't put it in the too hard basket - it just hasn't been an urgent priority up until now as it's coming up to the reporting period date. I will touch base with Kieren and have cc'ed him into this email to see what we can do. In terms of the record keeping - we would never expect you to guess, and it is a lot simpler than it sounds. Most of it is things that you would already have had to collect and would have given to your accountant eg. invoices for expenses such as seed and fertilizer, livestock numbers, fuel used ect. The main thing that the regulator needs is proof that you have changed practices in some way and that you have implemented what you said you would. They don't need extreme detail of every little thing that you have done on farm. If you would find it helpful, I can jump on a call with you and we can look at your map, go through what you've done on your project, what records you have, and put together a bit of a plan/list of what you need to proceed and get this done. Let me know and we can lock in a time to do that. Talk soon. If you need anything feel free to call me anytime. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Greenhill Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Sonya and Fraser, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project, Greenhill Carbon Project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you would be happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the next few weeks? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding the resampling process. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I will call within the next few days to discuss your results and project, but if you have any other questions feel free to reach out to myself or any other member of the AgriProve team. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Fraser, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. engagements.subject: Soil Sampling Results
engagements.body: Good Morning Fraser, Apologies for the delay on receiving your sampling results. I have attached the results to this email. As you will see, there has not been a measured increase in soil carbon in this sampling round for either of your projects. While this may be disappointing, it is important to remember that soil carbon projects are a long-term investment, with increase in SOC often taking a long time to be achieved. For next steps: 1. I have been talking to Christophe about locking in a time for someone from AgriProve to go through the HORIZON model with the both of you - I will coordinate that in a separate email. 1. We also have the option for you to chat to our grazier in residence who is able to give you some insight on grazing practices that promote soil carbon sequestration. If you would like to talk to him let me know and I will arrange a time for you with him. Any questions let me know. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Greenhill Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Sonya and Fraser, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project, Greenhill Carbon Project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you would be happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the next few weeks? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding the resampling process. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I will call within the next few days to discuss your results and project, but if you have any other questions feel free to reach out to myself or any other member of the AgriProve team. engagements.subject: Soil Sampling Results
engagements.body: Good Morning Fraser, Apologies for the delay on receiving your sampling results. I have attached the results to this email. As you will see, there has not been a measured increase in soil carbon in this sampling round for either of your projects. While this may be disappointing, it is important to remember that soil carbon projects are a long-term investment, with increase in SOC often taking a long time to be achieved. For next steps: 1. I have been talking to Christophe about locking in a time for someone from AgriProve to go through the HORIZON model with the both of you - I will coordinate that in a separate email. 1. We also have the option for you to chat to our grazier in residence who is able to give you some insight on grazing practices that promote soil carbon sequestration. If you would like to talk to him let me know and I will arrange a time for you with him. Any questions let me know. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note this is not a bad thing or indicative of if things are going backwards, it just means that there hasn't been enough positive change yet to justify resampling, which is to be expected as your project is not even 12 months old. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tony, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note this is not a bad thing or indicative of if things are going backwards, it just means that there hasn't been enough positive change yet to justify resampling, which is to be expected as your project is not even 12 months old. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Christophe, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? See my link below. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lyne CP
engagements.body: Dear Peter, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Draft Sampling Plans
engagements.body: Hi Michael, Please find attached the draft sampling plans for your carbon projects. Can you please review these plans with the following questions in mind: Are all project areas included? Are any areas included where the new activity will not be carried out? Are all obstacles such as buildings, dams, large trees, roads, steep slopes or other features that would prevent the new activity or soil sampling, excluded from the project areas? Are all sample points accessible by a vehicle? Soil sampling will be attempted to >1m. Are there any obstacles such as rocks or assets such as power, phone, gas, water or irrigation lines, which may affect sampling? Please note that the sample locations shown are indicative only. The final sample locations are randomly generated and may occur anywhere within the project area, and as such it is important that any areas where sampling cannot physically occur be excluded from the project. An AgriProve representative will be in touch over the coming days to finalise the draft plans. For your records, please also see attached Baseline Condition Report for this project area on your property, which is a requirement under our Universal Land Management Strategy (LMS). The LMS details how AgriProve uses satellite derived Normalised Difference Red Edge (NDRE) data, a measure of chlorophyll concentration in plants, to monitor material improvements to the NDRE based on eligible land management practices. Your projects have been registered with the regulator. Please note the assessment process can take approximately 90 days from lodgment to the project being officially declared as an ERF project by the CER. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Draft Sampling Plans
engagements.body: Hi Michael, For projects that have a total property size over 300 hectares, we register the property as multiple projects. This is done for several reasons including: * Increasing the probability that a project will have credits issued by aligning project areas with management zones * Allowing flexibility in sampling schedules across a property, for examples one project area may be resampled after 2 years, and another after 3 due to the annual review results * Mitigating risks associated with property sale whereby single parcels or land titles of a property are sold When splitting a property there are a number of factors that we take into consideration. These include: * Land title configuration. * Management areas. Different parts of a property may be managed differently and may respond differently to the application of eligible activities. * Soil variability and topography * Exclusion zones * We aim to register projects of approximately 100-200 hectares in size. The ‘Carbon Estimation Area’ or CEA is defined as the areas of the property where the project mechanism is to be implemented and must be tied to a land management strategy, including at least one new or materially different eligible activity, carried out on the land as part of the soil carbon project until the end of the permanence period. In defining the CEAs, considerations include: * Cadastral parcels * Paddock mapping/fence lines * Farm management zones * Soil type * Topography If you feel that the project split is better aligned with those paddocks that you provided in your email, based on these paddocks as management areas. I will redo the project split based on those paddocks and send back to you for confirmation. I can then continue to map the draft sampling plans, which includes mapping the Exclusion Zones, CEAs and Strata. Please feel free to contact me on the details below to discuss. Warm regards, Imogen Hickey | Crediting Specialist AgriProve Pty Ltd Phone: 1300 46 7645 Mobile: +61 402 509 303 Email: imogen@agriprove.io Address: Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. Can you please confirm that you would like to go ahead with the project split as discussed? engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Michael and Michelle, We have just completed your first annual review on your carbon projects. We do this by looking at Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) satellite data of your farm. This measures the vegetation trends on your farm in the past year to give us an indicator of if carbon sequestration has been likely to occur. We use this to decide if your project would be worthwhile resampling this year. I have attached your results showing your NDRE trend for the past year and the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. These results show that there has not been an increase in the average NDRE since baselining and therefore has not met our threshold to be resampled this year. We will review this again next year. Note: this does not mean carbon has gone backwards, It is showing you the vegetation trends and we use that as an indicator or what is likely to be happening in the ground. To tick off your review requirements for this year- we need to do a quick check in call where we run through what you have been doing in your project areas and then we have completed your annual review for the year. Is there a time this week or next that would suit to call and go through this? engagements.subject: AgriProve - Draft Sampling Plans
engagements.body: Hi Michael, Please find attached the draft sampling plans for your carbon projects. Can you please review these plans with the following questions in mind: Are all project areas included? Are any areas included where the new activity will not be carried out? Are all obstacles such as buildings, dams, large trees, roads, steep slopes or other features that would prevent the new activity or soil sampling, excluded from the project areas? Are all sample points accessible by a vehicle? Soil sampling will be attempted to >1m. Are there any obstacles such as rocks or assets such as power, phone, gas, water or irrigation lines, which may affect sampling? Please note that the sample locations shown are indicative only. The final sample locations are randomly generated and may occur anywhere within the project area, and as such it is important that any areas where sampling cannot physically occur be excluded from the project. An AgriProve representative will be in touch over the coming days to finalise the draft plans. For your records, please also see attached Baseline Condition Report for this project area on your property, which is a requirement under our Universal Land Management Strategy (LMS). The LMS details how AgriProve uses satellite derived Normalised Difference Red Edge (NDRE) data, a measure of chlorophyll concentration in plants, to monitor material improvements to the NDRE based on eligible land management practices. Your projects have been registered with the regulator. Please note the assessment process can take approximately 90 days from lodgment to the project being officially declared as an ERF project by the CER. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Michael and Michelle, We have just completed your first annual review on your carbon projects. We do this by looking at Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) satellite data of your farm. This measures the vegetation trends on your farm in the past year to give us an indicator of if carbon sequestration has been likely to occur. We use this to decide if your project would be worthwhile resampling this year. I have attached your results showing your NDRE trend for the past year and the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. These results show that there has not been an increase in the average NDRE since baselining and therefore has not met our threshold to be resampled this year. We will review this again next year. Note: this does not mean carbon has gone backwards, It is showing you the vegetation trends and we use that as an indicator or what is likely to be happening in the ground. To tick off your review requirements for this year- we need to do a quick check in call where we run through what you have been doing in your project areas and then we have completed your annual review for the year. Is there a time this week or next that would suit to call and go through this? engagements.subject: AgriProve - Draft Sampling Plans
engagements.body: Hi Michael, Please find attached the draft sampling plans for your carbon projects. Can you please review these plans with the following questions in mind: Are all project areas included? Are any areas included where the new activity will not be carried out? Are all obstacles such as buildings, dams, large trees, roads, steep slopes or other features that would prevent the new activity or soil sampling, excluded from the project areas? Are all sample points accessible by a vehicle? Soil sampling will be attempted to >1m. Are there any obstacles such as rocks or assets such as power, phone, gas, water or irrigation lines, which may affect sampling? Please note that the sample locations shown are indicative only. The final sample locations are randomly generated and may occur anywhere within the project area, and as such it is important that any areas where sampling cannot physically occur be excluded from the project. An AgriProve representative will be in touch over the coming days to finalise the draft plans. For your records, please also see attached Baseline Condition Report for this project area on your property, which is a requirement under our Universal Land Management Strategy (LMS). The LMS details how AgriProve uses satellite derived Normalised Difference Red Edge (NDRE) data, a measure of chlorophyll concentration in plants, to monitor material improvements to the NDRE based on eligible land management practices. Your projects have been registered with the regulator. Please note the assessment process can take approximately 90 days from lodgment to the project being officially declared as an ERF project by the CER. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Michael and Michelle, We have just completed your first annual review on your carbon projects. We do this by looking at Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) satellite data of your farm. This measures the vegetation trends on your farm in the past year to give us an indicator of if carbon sequestration has been likely to occur. We use this to decide if your project would be worthwhile resampling this year. I have attached your results showing your NDRE trend for the past year and the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. These results show that there has not been an increase in the average NDRE since baselining and therefore has not met our threshold to be resampled this year. We will review this again next year. Note: this does not mean carbon has gone backwards, It is showing you the vegetation trends and we use that as an indicator or what is likely to be happening in the ground. To tick off your review requirements for this year- we need to do a quick check in call where we run through what you have been doing in your project areas and then we have completed your annual review for the year. Is there a time this week or next that would suit to call and go through this? engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 - Farm Management Records
engagements.body: Hi Leonie and David, Thank you for returning the management records document. Regarding the possibility of relinquishment of ACCUs in the event of sale and the incoming owners electing not to continue the project. AgriProve’s Master Terms and Conditions addresses this in the event of sale. Clause 2.7 states that “if Operator is to cease being the operator of any Project Property, Landholder and Operator agree to notify AgriProve as soon as they are aware and to novate this agreement…” This means that the incoming buyers would need to (for the purposes of the project) become the Operator and the project continues. If, however, they would like to cease “implementation” of the project, then they would notify AgriProve of their intent to cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities as per clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions. They would then allow AgriProve to come to the property and complete the required soil testing to ensure we meet our reporting obligations to keep the project registered and compliant with the ERF. This would mean, in all operational aspects, that as long as the land remained in an agricultural system, and this process is followed, that the project is no longer ‘active’ (in the form of implementation), however it is still compliant to the ERF. This indemnifies both the outgoing landholder and incoming landholder of any requirement to relinquish ACCUs. Furthermore, there is no cost obligation to the incoming landholder, as AgriProve bears the costs of any subsequent sampling, auditing requirements, and reporting/administrative requirements for the project. Hope that answers the query appropriately, please let me know if you require more information. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 ACCU Issuance
engagements.body: Hi Leonie, I think that you are referring to the cash prepayment option for ACCU distribution, where AgriProve makes a cash prepayment for ACCUs to the project operator in advance of the ACCUs being generated at a fixed price of $12.50 per ACCU. This option would be selected at the start of the carbon project in the Sale and Licence Agreement and is based on the prepayment to AgriProve at an agreed price of $12.50 for ACCUs from a buyer. Based on your selection of option 3 in the Sale and Licence Agreement to 'hold ACCUs for future sale', your ACCUs will be held in AgriProve's Registry of Emissions Units Account (ANREAU) on trust for sale at a later date nominated by you for the best price available. AgriProve will act as a market broker for the ACCUs, and a brokerage fee of $0.375 per ACCU will be charged. These ACCUs could also be transferred to the Operators stand-alone ANREU account if established. engagements.subject: Leonie Doran and Hobbs Catch up
Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Ryan CPs
engagements.body: Dear Leonie and David, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 - Farm Management Records
engagements.body: Hi Leonie and David, Thank you for returning the management records document. Regarding the possibility of relinquishment of ACCUs in the event of sale and the incoming owners electing not to continue the project. AgriProve’s Master Terms and Conditions addresses this in the event of sale. Clause 2.7 states that “if Operator is to cease being the operator of any Project Property, Landholder and Operator agree to notify AgriProve as soon as they are aware and to novate this agreement…” This means that the incoming buyers would need to (for the purposes of the project) become the Operator and the project continues. If, however, they would like to cease “implementation” of the project, then they would notify AgriProve of their intent to cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities as per clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions. They would then allow AgriProve to come to the property and complete the required soil testing to ensure we meet our reporting obligations to keep the project registered and compliant with the ERF. This would mean, in all operational aspects, that as long as the land remained in an agricultural system, and this process is followed, that the project is no longer ‘active’ (in the form of implementation), however it is still compliant to the ERF. This indemnifies both the outgoing landholder and incoming landholder of any requirement to relinquish ACCUs. Furthermore, there is no cost obligation to the incoming landholder, as AgriProve bears the costs of any subsequent sampling, auditing requirements, and reporting/administrative requirements for the project. Hope that answers the query appropriately, please let me know if you require more information. engagements.subject: Ryan Carbon Project 2 ACCU Issuance
engagements.body: Good morning Leonie and David, Congratulations on your recent ACCU issuance for Ryan Carbon Project 2 and thank you for your patience. Now that your ACCUs have been issued, please see the attached Draft Statement of Account for Ryan Carbon Project 1 and 2. The statement shows the breakdown of the ACCU distribution after accounting for the AgriProve success fee and any elected deferred payments for baseline soil sampling. The statement outlines the following areas: * AgriProve Carbon Project Licence Fee due to Client (Agriprove pays $1 per year to you as a landholder for the 30 year Carbon Project period) * The ACCUs Issuance * Balance of ACCUs after Agriprove Success Fee (25% success fee on total ACCUs issued) * Balance of Baseline Soil Sampling cost across all projects * ACCU Distribution preference (as outlined in the KCT) Please also see the attached bank details request form. We require this information to pay the $30 (excl. GST) licence fee to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon project for the term of the agreement. We will also require this information to pay out the proceeds from any future sale of ACCUs on your behalf. Please feel free to give me a call to go through the statement over the phone to make sure the distributions are understood and address any questions you may have. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 ACCU Issuance
engagements.body: Hi Leonie, I think that you are referring to the cash prepayment option for ACCU distribution, where AgriProve makes a cash prepayment for ACCUs to the project operator in advance of the ACCUs being generated at a fixed price of $12.50 per ACCU. This option would be selected at the start of the carbon project in the Sale and Licence Agreement and is based on the prepayment to AgriProve at an agreed price of $12.50 for ACCUs from a buyer. Based on your selection of option 3 in the Sale and Licence Agreement to 'hold ACCUs for future sale', your ACCUs will be held in AgriProve's Registry of Emissions Units Account (ANREAU) on trust for sale at a later date nominated by you for the best price available. AgriProve will act as a market broker for the ACCUs, and a brokerage fee of $0.375 per ACCU will be charged. These ACCUs could also be transferred to the Operators stand-alone ANREU account if established. Sent email to notify Leonie her emissions data had been fixed in the platform Hi Leonie & David, Thanks for your patience. I’ve now updated your account with stock movements that we went through together 2 weeks ago. We’ve fixed the issues with weights and the emissions outputs are now looking a lot better. Here’s a snapshot I took of your emissions page. You’ll notice Emissions Intensity for beef are on the low side (which is good)- a typical regen beef operation will run at 9-12kg CO2/Kg liveweight compared to say, 12-18kg CO2/Kg LW for a feedlot operation so you’re doing well! I suspect it might come up a bit once we start adding years before and after to smooth out the end of year trading. Sheep meat Emissions Intensity is about average (typically 6-12kg CO2kg LW) but again I think we’d see some smoothing out as your trading was right at the end of the year and including the following year would give us some more accuracy. Your Scope 1+ 2 emissions are correct and can be used for reporting to any downstream suppliers if that’s what you're intending to do. Look out for more updates in the coming weeks as we add status reporting for your Carbon Project. Also, regarding your ACCUs balance- this is the total issuance form the ACCU scheme and doesn’t include AgriProve’s portion. We’re looking at adding a ‘wallet’ feature in the future that splits these numbers out and tracks subsequent issuance and spend eg, with Clima. We let you know when this becomes available. Any other questions please feel free to reach out to myself or Claudia. Regards,

engagements.subject: Leonie Doran and Hobbs Catch up
Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Ryan CPs
engagements.body: Dear Leonie and David, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes set-up and next steps
engagements.body: Good morning Karen, Welcome to the Tags for Tonnes team!! We are proud and excited to offer a world-first initiative such as this to assist with your carbon project management. Now that we have your tags on the way, we are progressing to have you set-up and ready by the time your tags arrive. Here is a short guide on how to operationalise your tags when you receive them: 1. The instructions will be on a small welcome card in your package - scan the QR code with your phone camera to access them. 2. Charging the tags in the sun is the first step to getting started (they will need to sit in the sun for 5-7 days to charge fully). 3. I have created an account for you in our software and have uploaded your farm boundaries in it. 4. We will need to jump on a video call so I can run you through how to connect your tags to our software - this will require making a Ceres Tag account in their portal, and registering your tags to our software (I will walk you through this step-by-step) . 5. Once your tags are charged and you are set-up in the software you are ready to tag 6. It is important to record as many details around which animal you are tagging (Ceres tag number, VID, NLIS ID, age) using what tag and what mob/class/breed they belong to. 7. Taking a picture of the animal is also an important step to help tell their story. 8. Once tagged, and the animal data is recorded we can jump on a call to set up your animal information in the 'My Herd' section of the software - this will power all the insights you can get on your herd's performance. 9. You are ready to go! When your tags have arrived, let me know and we can organise our first video call. Any questions you may have please feel free to reach out to me. We are excited to start this new chapter of carbon farming with you! Hi Karen, I hope you are going well! I am filling out the co-benefits report for LRF to unlock the payment. I was wondering if you could please fill gaps and expand on my answers to bold questions below, and provide any additional photos on management activities (grazing, weed control, sowing, fencing). The report is for the period of the 1/11/2022 to 1/11/2023. Weed management - Please provide details on this activity undertaken during the reporting period. Include as much information as possible, including location and size of the area where the activity has occurred, the frequency and in which months, include any planned works that did not take place and reasons why. * Weed management was conducted across the property by both the landholders and contractors. Contractors completed approximately 52 hours of weed management plus additional hours by the landholders. Chemical application was conducted to control highest priority weeds; Cats claw, Giant rats tail grass and Lantana. Chemical weed control was conducted in line with Land Management Report. Did you do any fire management as well? Stock management in remnant areas - Please provide details on this activity undertaken during the reporting period. Include as much information as possible, including location and size of the area where the activity has occurred, the frequency and in which months, include any planned works that did not take place and reasons why. Remnant vegetation areas have been fenced off with X km fence installed and X new troughs. Remnant areas have been carefully grazed according to Land Management Report. Holistic grazing management was implemented providing project areas with sufficient rest periods to enable full recovery of plants and root mass, maximising soil carbon. Grazing has been conducted rotationally for short durations X days, X times per year, allowing X rest. Grazing is conducted based on feed availability to reduce impact on native trees and shrubs. Stock are removed so there is always 100% groundcover remaining. Smaller areas are fenced off using electric tape to enable rotational grazing. Currently paddock sizes are 100ha but we are looking to reduce this using (electric) tape to avoid grazing too heavily’. Stock management in riparian areas - Please provide details on this activity undertaken during the reporting period. Include as much information as possible, including location and size of the area where the activity has occurred, the frequency and in which months, include any planned works that did not take place and reasons why. XX km of waterways and riparian zones on the property have been fenced off to keep stock out and to rehabilitate waterways, to slow water and prevent erosion and runoff. Fencing of all riparian corridors X km fencing with X troughs installed. Grazing has been conducted according to Land Management Report. Grazing has only been conducted in riparian zones as crash grazing/short duration grazing once per year. Grazing density is determined based on feed availability. Stock are removed so that there is always 100% groundcover remaining to avoid bare ground and erosion. Grazing has only been conducted in riparian zones when conditions are dry. Photos: Do you have any photos of: -Weed management -Stock restriction/grazing in remnant or riparian zones? -photos of the work or work done by the man you hired? -Any other photos of work completed (eg fencing/water). Thankyou! Melanie

engagements.subject: Interview for AgriProve Carbon Builders
engagements.body: Hi Karen, It was lovely speaking to you yesterday and learning more about your operation. I have written a draft of what we would like to post in the AgriProve Carbon Builders group on Facebook, I will pop it down below in this email. If you could give it a read and send back if you have any concerns or thoughts with it that would be amazing please. We are happy to alter and change things if you are not comfortable sharing certain pieces of information. We would also love to tag you in the post as well, is this something you would be comfortable with? Here is the draft: "Afternoon Carbon Builders! This week we have an insight to another one of our members, Karen Scanlan from Kenmay Station. She spoke in an interview to the changes made in management and the most prominent results observed. Bio and carbon project: Karen and her husband Robert run a cattle operation in the Gladstone region of Queensland and have been involved in a carbon project since 2020. Their main motivations for starting a carbon project were to improve the environment and increase both flora and fauna diversity to integrate wildlife with cattle. Natural capital: In conjunction with their soil carbon project, they have an Accounting for Nature project that measures natural capital (co-benefits). The improvements to management have been measured, packaged and sold to the Queensland Government through the Land Restoration Fund. See more about their project here: https://www.accountingfornature.org/auacc56 Previous management: Through strategic management and infrastructure development they have been able to transform the property from being run down due to set stocking and lack of active management to a thriving landscape. Management conversion: They have made considerable improvements to the property in terms of fencing infrastructure with internal fences and laneways to assist with rotational grazing. They now are able to run 320 head of cattle through nine paddocks to allow for pasture rejuvenation. Multi-species perennial pastures have been sowed to increase biodiversity and biomass to reduce run off into the Great Barrier Reef. Their future plans are to further develop their fencing infrastructure to extend the rest periods and continue to improve pastures. Results: As a result, they have been able to quadruple their carrying capacity and have an increased body of pasture in height and species diversity. Education: Karen has utilised several educational courses and personal experience to create the current and future management plans. Some of these courses were Holistic Management, pasture improvement, and cattle trading, with the greatest influence being Joel Salatin's enterprise stacking method." Thank you so much for you time and looking forward to hearing from you! engagements.subject: CERES TAG data issue update
engagements.body: Good evening Karen, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since early April from your CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Re: Fysh Project
engagements.body: Hi Claudia To answer your questions; 1. Grazing in riparian areas Cattle did not graze at all in riparian areas along waterways. In our three larger paddocks with remenant vegetation, cattle were withheld from November 2024 to the start of March 2025. For the other 8 months of the year cattle were rotated two weeks in and three months rest. This means that the cattle grazed the riparian areas for approximately 6 weeks during the year. 2. Sewing improved pasture In March 2025 30 hectares beside Baffle Creek was sewn to improved pasture. The seed mix consisted of humidicola, signal and rhodes grass. 3.Employees and contractors My husband and I employ two local contractors. One lives on the farm. They each work approximately 20 hours per week. Their primary tasks are weed control and slashing pasture. 4. Rainfall The rainfall over the past year was average, with increased frequency of showers. This was similar to last year. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Karen, I am getting in touch as I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. We complete this review each year to determine if we think re-sampling your carbon project would be worthwhile. This review uses satellite imagery to determine if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. This means that we will potentially resample your project this year as it has demonstrated positive indicators. To confirm this, we will now run your project through an additional model and complete an implementation check over the phone. Once we have that information, we can confirm if we will be resampling this year or not. Is there a time that suits you in the next few weeks to complete this review over the phone? Talk soon. engagements.body: Hi Kylie and Lance, In preparation for the Site Visit on Tuesday 11th June, I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. Please see the attached agenda for the site visit, and a couple of aspects that will be discussed as well as the following questions. 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of FMR dates) 2. Detailed description of all lad management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the property, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to house/office - interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall, the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that management records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the management records such as livestock records and grazing charts * Confirmation that we (yourselves and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the carbon project operation, implementation and administration. Please reach out if you have any questions. Have a good weekend. engagements.subject: Ceres Tag data issues update
engagements.body: Dear Kylie and Lance, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since early April from your CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Questions from today regarding sustainability certifications
engagements.body: Good evening Lance and Kylie. Thank you for being so generous with your time today, I really appreciate it. As mentioned below are some of the questions we ran through, if you have anything to add please feel free to put them in and send them back. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? No, just organic stuff – don’t qualify (don’t breed, buy in and keep for under 2 years) They trade too much and not enough breeders – gotta have the cattle for more than 2 years Looked into it 10 years ago If no, then why not? Just haven’t got to it because of not meeting the organic cert qualification Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? No, haven’t looked into more Grass resilient certification have heard Reef credits – interested post development Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? Is ideal for them and they are very open to it They are practicing no hormone and non-synthetic feed Very, very interested Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? Quite interested as long as it doesn’t cost too much Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? Have looked at retailers Sell to Meat Works - shop around for pricing Go for premium price MSA Private sales – bulls (stud premiums) More for the quality than the environmental – organic is the only option (gone off that) Has enquired at beef expos for Auction Plus – is the way to go in the future (AI) – photos of property and cattle – price of putting on Auctions Plus is dearer than selling through the (Meat) Works but price is coming down Gotta have time to look at it properly – but has been very interested for the past 10-12 years What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? They are pretty well up there already More in the soils – more testing of soils to see what is lacking in soils Educating them on what the results mean and how to adapt and improve their place Some education and making the reports easy to understand We give a lot of information and they don’t know how to interpret Pointing out what is missing in the soils and how to improve using the tests we have done Microbial analysis to drive the limiting factors – key factor Thank you! engagements.subject: Soil Carbon Project Annual Remote Assessment Results
engagements.body: Hi Lance and Kylie, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your projects, Duncan Carbon Projects 1 & 2. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. Since the increase from the baseline to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. As part of our six-monthly reviews, I'd love to call you some time in the next two weeks to check in and see how your projects are doing. Would either this Friday (17th) or next Tuesday (21st) suit? Feel free to reach out if you have any other questions or concerns about your soil carbon projects. engagements.subject: ACCU's Follow Up
engagements.body: Good Morning Kylie, Thanks for your call last week. I have followed up with our team about your ACCU's and next steps. Your ACCU's were issued on the 19th September last year (2025). You were issued 5773 ACCUS and after our percentage is removed your entitlement is 4330 ACCU's. The next steps are you need to set up your ANREU account so that we can transfer them over to you and you can manage your ACCU's in your own account going forwards. There is also the option for you to sell some of these ACCU's. If you would like more information and for me to look into that for you, let me know. To set up your ANREU account: We can do it for you, but it requires entering all of your identity documentation and so it can be easier for you to do it yourself and call us if you have any questions along the way. engagements.subject: Ceres Tag data issues update
engagements.body: Dear Kylie and Lance, I’d like to provide an update on the data matter appearing since early April from your CERES RANCH Tags. We were the first to report an issue showing our diligence and care towards your projects. In summary, in March 2024, CERES TAG had firmware updated with a new design from CSIRO to improve battery life, accuracy, reliability and flexibility to update with additional algorithms. The Pasture Feed Intake (PFI) was not anticipated to operate differently from the previous firmware on this updated and improved model, however this was not the case. The team at CERES TAG and CSIRO are working to remedy the algorithm now to restore to performance equivalent to that pre-March. This week a patch fix was deployed to in-field testing. There is no issue with the GPS location data. Your animal location monitoring is unaffected. As we learn more about their progress towards a resolution, we will keep you informed. We thank you for your support, understanding and patience. If you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Questions from today regarding sustainability certifications
engagements.body: Good evening Lance and Kylie. Thank you for being so generous with your time today, I really appreciate it. As mentioned below are some of the questions we ran through, if you have anything to add please feel free to put them in and send them back. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? No, just organic stuff – don’t qualify (don’t breed, buy in and keep for under 2 years) They trade too much and not enough breeders – gotta have the cattle for more than 2 years Looked into it 10 years ago If no, then why not? Just haven’t got to it because of not meeting the organic cert qualification Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? No, haven’t looked into more Grass resilient certification have heard Reef credits – interested post development Would you want to explore the criteria to have a sustainability certification applied to your produce? Is ideal for them and they are very open to it They are practicing no hormone and non-synthetic feed Very, very interested Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? Quite interested as long as it doesn’t cost too much Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? Have looked at retailers Sell to Meat Works - shop around for pricing Go for premium price MSA Private sales – bulls (stud premiums) More for the quality than the environmental – organic is the only option (gone off that) Has enquired at beef expos for Auction Plus – is the way to go in the future (AI) – photos of property and cattle – price of putting on Auctions Plus is dearer than selling through the (Meat) Works but price is coming down Gotta have time to look at it properly – but has been very interested for the past 10-12 years What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? They are pretty well up there already More in the soils – more testing of soils to see what is lacking in soils Educating them on what the results mean and how to adapt and improve their place Some education and making the reports easy to understand We give a lot of information and they don’t know how to interpret Pointing out what is missing in the soils and how to improve using the tests we have done Microbial analysis to drive the limiting factors – key factor Thank you! Kind regards, Dylan Cronje | Innovation Project Co-Ordinator Phone: 0419940230: tel:%7bPhone%7d Mobile: 0419940230: tel:%7bMobile%7d Email: dylan@agriprove.io: mailto:william@agriprove.io Address: Level 1/601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 www.agriprove.io: https://agriprove.io/ : https://www.linkedin.com/company/user_name_here: https://www.linkedin.com/company/agriprove-pty-ltd/ : https://www.facebook.com/agriprove1/ : https://www.twitter.com/agriprove : https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCj6-LPG2-c5h5RUn5u8SuZw Here at AgriProve PTY LTD we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Soil Carbon Project Annual Remote Assessment Results
engagements.body: Hi Lance and Kylie, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your projects, Duncan Carbon Projects 1 & 2. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. Since the increase from the baseline to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. As part of our six-monthly reviews, I'd love to call you some time in the next two weeks to check in and see how your projects are doing. Would either this Friday (17th) or next Tuesday (21st) suit? Feel free to reach out if you have any other questions or concerns about your soil carbon projects. engagements.subject: ACCU's Follow Up
engagements.body: Good Morning Kylie, Thanks for your call last week. I have followed up with our team about your ACCU's and next steps. Your ACCU's were issued on the 19th September last year (2025). You were issued 5773 ACCUS and after our percentage is removed your entitlement is 4330 ACCU's. The next steps are you need to set up your ANREU account so that we can transfer them over to you and you can manage your ACCU's in your own account going forwards. There is also the option for you to sell some of these ACCU's. If you would like more information and for me to look into that for you, let me know. To set up your ANREU account: We can do it for you, but it requires entering all of your identity documentation and so it can be easier for you to do it yourself and call us if you have any questions along the way. We can also book in a time to go through it over the phone with you if you need. engagements.subject: ANREU Account
engagements.body: Good Morning Kylie, I have checked in with Will, and he has suggested that the mistake may have been you clicked on the NGER form instead of the ANREU form. To get to it when you sign into your online services account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/) , you type in ANREU in search and select the ANREU form. Here is a photo of what I am talking about. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Result
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jodie, As discussed, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. This review uses satellite imagery to determine if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. This means that we will potentially resample your project this year as it has demonstrated positive indicators. To confirm this, we will now run your project through an additional model and complete your implementation check over the phone. Once we have that information, we can confirm if we will be resampling this year. Is there a time that suits you in the next few weeks to complete this review over the phone? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Re: Rohanclaire Farming Project- more questions
Re: Rohanclaire Farming Project- more questions
engagements.body: Hi Laura, Thank you very much for reaching out with these clarification questions. I have detailed some responses below but if you would like more information please don’t hesitate to reach out. We are currently destocked due to very limited water availability on the property at the moment (thanks to virtually missing last yrs wet season). Does this restrict our time-frame for the project? EG if baseline sampling is completed, and we can't purchase cattle for another 12 months, does our project actually start when we get the cattle or when we do the baseline? You’ll be happy to hear that the method has been written to account for climatic variability and real-world circumstances when considering things like destocking events. A destocking event does not restrict the timeframe for the project. Provided you intend to keep the property under an agricultural system long term, a destocking event for the reason of limited water availability is completely reasonable. As long as there is real intention to restock, if this takes 2 years due to drought and then financial consideration etc. that is also ok. We would, however, hold off resampling until the eligible activities have been conducted. If this is establishment of pasture or a change in grazing management, we would ensure these practice changes have occurred prior to resampling as if we were to measure an increase, it is a requirement of the method that the eligible activities have taken place between sampling rounds. So, a destocking period extending another 12 months may simply extend the timeframe between resampling. Please note we must re-sample at least once within a five year period to maintain compliance so a least one eligible activity (e.g. Change in grazing management) must be implemented across the project area during this time. For clarification, project start date is when the project is declared. Declaration occurs within 90 days of project registration assuming no requests for further information. The baseline soil sampling can occur any time within 18month from the initial project registration. If we want to develop a small section of the trial plot within the 25 yrs, can we section it off down the track? Eg after 10 yrs of the project? There are a few ways we can manage this for you. Firstly, we would look to understand what the trial plot will be used for. If it is still under some type of agricultural production considered by the method, and the trial works links to an eligible activity then we can leave it under project. Otherwise, if you know the area you intend to use, we can leave it out of project. Alternatively, we could section this area off as its own Carbon Estimation Area (CEA). CEAs are subcomponents of a project area and can be dropped out of a project without impacting the rest of the project. Should you decide to turn the area into a trial plot we can drop this section out of project. To drop a CEA out of project any credits generated on that area would have to be relinquished by the landholder. There are also flexibilities within the method that allows a few hectares to be built on per CEA without needing to drop the CEA out of project which will also provide another option for dealing with changes in land use. So basically, not a problem. We can work with you on this! We would like to have confirmation that we are actually in control of our stocking rate based on feed or water availability or personal circumstances. If for example we would like to completely destock for 3-6 months for a holiday, finances or some other reason, are we able to do so? I'm assuming here that we would have to have a backup plan to ensure that we restock within a certain timeframe? Yes, all stocking rate changes (increases or decreases) are in your complete control. Provided there is a reason to completely destock for a period of time, such as all of those listed above, and an intention to restock, then that won’t be a problem for the project. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Result
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Laura, I am getting in touch as I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. We complete this review each year to determine if we think re-sampling your carbon project would be worthwhile. This review uses satellite imagery to determine if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. As you will see in the attached document, your projects' average NDRE has had a positive trend when compared to the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. This means that we will potentially resample your project this year as it has demonstrated positive indicators. To confirm this, we will now run your project through an additional model and complete an implementation check over the phone. Once we have that information, we can confirm if we will be resampling this year or not. Is there a time that suits you in the next few weeks to complete this review over the phone? Talk soon. 25/26 Annual Review Call Playbook Have they been informed of and seen their LIA results? Yes Notes: Were surprised as thought it would be pretty flat. Have had a good start to the season but was dry before that. Have they been informed of the next steps and timeline for resampling? Yes Notes: Told her It will go through the model and be in touch in next few months. Did everything go as planned and you got what you wanted to done? Yes Notes: 150mm rainfall in past few months before that was very dry. For each project ask them: - What did they do in these areas in the past year? - When? - Exact products/species? - percentage of project area for each? Notes: At the time of starting this project they had destocked and had no stock to allow grass to recover. They now have 63 head of cattle (heifers 200-280kg) that are rotational grazing the area. This means a stocking rate alteration has occurred on 100% of the property. All their infrastructure for grazing was completed before the project, but the high intensity grazing began after starting the project. High density grazing is their main focus, but they are putting out seed to improve pastures too. They are currently putting out after the cattle have grazed an area. Have you noticed any really positive changes on ground? (Id so would happy to send photos) and then possibly share with us on group. Notes: They are noticing a lot of increase water holding and effective rainfall as their pastures are capturing rainfall effectively and staying wetter for longer. Have they completed any of the below activities? - Tree Clearing - Building of additional infrastructure - Tree Plantings - Land Sale If so outline the details below. Yes Notes: planted some trees - 23kms of contouring in recently- planting on top of the contours. Have you had any of the below natural disasters or unforeseen circumstances? - Fire - Flooding no Do you have records to show these things happening? eg. grazing charts, activity logs , pocket books, spreadsheets ect. Notes: mostly spreadsheets- cattle one and diesel usage, Have you logged onto the online platform yet? Yes If they answer YES to being on the platform: 1. What did you think of it? 2. Do they have any suggestion of what they would like to see it do in future or ways it could improve at the moment? Notes: The mapping was a bit out of date, a lot of potential , Didn't see our data but may have been user error, Likes that its integrated with acceredtation-s they like that - she has accreditations, Is there anything your struggling with around your carbon project at the moment? Notes: no - just clarifying points and now feel better. Now compliments day How satisfied are you with AgriProve? 4 -Satisfied Notes: 4.5 - always available and helpful. How likely would you be on a scale 1-10 to recommend AgriProve to a friend that wants to do a carbon project? 10 Notes: I have already. 3 people that i've spoken to already. They were receptive and listening but not that happy to jump in themselves.

engagements.subject: Re: Ellis - Carbon update
engagements.body: Good Morning Laura, I can see that your project is in the Tn Sampling phase which suggests that it is still on the list to be sampled. There has been a bit of a delay getting soil sampling contractors and we are also about to do a schedule 2 round of crediting in Queensland. What this means is we will be able to credit based on our model predictions - which your model result is currently indicating an increase. How this works is we will put together what are called reference groups, the regulator randomly chooses 10% of them to physically sample and then based on those results the model is calibrated and you will be able to be issued credits based on the model's predictions. I assume that your project will be a part of this and that is why there has been a hold up on sampling. I will check in with the team to make sure, but we will be pulling these together to be done in June - September, so expect someone to be in touch around those times. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review Result
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Alan, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon projects. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks? Tuesday or Wednesday next week would be ideal, but happy to work around you.
