engagements.subject: AgriProve - Process changes impacting projects registered after 8th November
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. I'll give you a call to makes sure you received my email and should you have any questions or need assistance, don’t hesitate to reach out. Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

Called to check in on KCT: It was still with solicitor and the solicitor had concerns. Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. The answers don't need to be long we just need to have some specifics to put in your application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.subject: AgriProve - Process changes impacting projects registered after 8th November
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. I'll give you a call to makes sure you received my email and should you have any questions or need assistance, don’t hesitate to reach out. Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Paul, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. If the average change is higher since baselining- that suggests soil carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred. As you will see in the attached document your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Record's & Update
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Paul, Thanks for your time on the phone today. As discussed, the next steps will be: 1. We are going to vary your start date till after your baseline period - This has no effect on you other than giving us all more time to get the records together for the 5-year deadline. This may also be an advantage as it will push out your sampling to April next year and it may not be as dry as it is now. 2. Early next year we will put your project through our new model to get a better indicator of if carbon sequestration has been likely and look to schedule your 5-year sampling. Our operations team will be in touch when that is done and they are organizing the logistics. ( I expect that to be in February/March). * 3. From Now we will start pulling together all of your records for you to complete the 5-year audit. There are a few steps to this, but as a start we need to get together your management history from before the baseline period and then now the 5 years since the project has started. TO GET STARTED WITH THE RECORDS: What we need to prove is that you have done things differently since commencing the project ( start date 19/01/2021) - focusing on your nutrient application, what you have sown and anything that could have improved carbon like lime, fencing and grazing management. To do this, we basically need WHAT was done, WHEN and WHERE. E.g. 50kg of Urea/ ha was applied to paddock 1 and 2 which is a total of 150 ha and ideally with evidence eg. receipts - the more detail the better as a change can be you used to apply 100kg and now you do 50kg, you used to apply it in 1 form and now you've put it out as something different, you used to sow oats and now you do a mix, you used to do a summer mix and since starting you've put in a winter mix ect. - the practice change doesn't need to be the same across your whole place, but something different does need to be shown across your whole project. So as a starting point: * if you could get together those rudimentary notes about what was done in each paddock over the time since you had the farm ( as detailed as possible like mentioned above) * A paddock map would be great if you have one ( can be simple drawn or photo ) so we can visually understand what has happened where from those notes. Once we have an idea of this - we can make a plan of attack and let you know what specific evidence you need. If you have any questions feel free to give me a call anytime. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Review Results
engagements.body: Good afternoon Rick, Looking forward to talking to you on Wednesday. I have just completed the satellite component of your carbon project annual reviews today. The documents attached are the results & I have summarized the outcomes below. What these graphs show is the NDRE change on your project areas overtime. We compare how this changed before the project started and then after to see if there has been an improvement in the average NDRE overtime. NDRE measures greenness and chlorophyll of your vegetation. If there has been an increase in the NDRE this is an indicator of potential carbon sequestration and is an indicator we use to decide if we should resample your projects each year. The results for your projects are below: Carrick Carbon Project 1: did not meet threshold for resampling Carrick Carbon Project 2: did not meet threshold for resampling Carrick Carbon Project 3: Close to threshold so will consider resampling. engagements.subject: Potential Sale of Carbon Project Area
engagements.body: Good Morning Andrew, Sorry it took me a while to get back to you. I am replying just to confirm some of the information discussed on the phone a few weeks ago around potentially selling the property Carrick Carbon projects are on. As discussed, as you don't currently have any credits, it would be fairly simple for us to revoke the Carrick projects if it was required. The best-case scenario, however, is that the new owners would like to take over the project. This works well for them as baseline costs are already covered and they would get to start and benefit from a project with no upfront costs for them. We are happy to do whatever is needed to help make this happen so if you would like some estimates to give to potential buyers or would like us to talk to anyone about what it means let us know, however we are able to revoke the project without penalty to you if they don't want to continue. The idea is to show what’s actually happening on the ground and how soil carbon projects turn into real outcomes for producers and the broader market. If you’re coming along, it’d be great to see you there or have a chat at the stand afterwards. All the best, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io On Sunday, 19 October 2025, 9:40:04 am +1100, Claudia Bryant wrote: Hi Andrew, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. Here’s the link if you’d like to check out the program: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/ Hope to see you there, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io

engagements.subject: Potential Sale of Carbon Project Area
engagements.body: Good Morning Andrew, Sorry it took me a while to get back to you. I am replying just to confirm some of the information discussed on the phone a few weeks ago around potentially selling the property Carrick Carbon projects are on. As discussed, as you don't currently have any credits, it would be fairly simple for us to revoke the Carrick projects if it was required. The best-case scenario, however, is that the new owners would like to take over the project. This works well for them as baseline costs are already covered and they would get to start and benefit from a project with no upfront costs for them. We are happy to do whatever is needed to help make this happen so if you would like some estimates to give to potential buyers or would like us to talk to anyone about what it means let us know, however we are able to revoke the project without penalty to you if they don't want to continue. Where are things on sale? Are you just exploring it or is this something that is happening currently? Kind Regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:492d8ae7-3d86-4e77-b518-f2abb216a0a3] [cid:b34b61a1-9235-441e-995b-0c947c97c1d2] [cid:7819e2cf-ebeb-45a3-ae1f-f7c7373ed480] [cid:cfbae698-2480-45f4-8e7c-bc540ac49ab7] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. If you have any questions related compliance or data protection, please contact our Data Protection Officer .
